About Charles River Associates

Charles River Associates is a leading global consulting firm that offers economic, financial, and strategic expertise to major law firms, corporations, and governments around the world.  CRA advises clients on economic and financial matters pertaining to litigation and regulatory proceedings, and guides corporations through critical business strategy and performance-related issues. Since 1965, clients have engaged CRA for its combination of industry experience and rigorous, fact-based analysis that provide clients with clear, implementable solutions to complex business concerns.

CRA's European Competition practice specialises in providing economic advice on matters of competition policy and regulation. We assist firms and their legal advisors in all types of competition proceedings before competition authorities and courts: mergers and acquisitions, abuse of dominance allegations, cartels, restrictive commercial agreements, market investigations, litigation and disputes, intellectual property or state aid. We also provide advice to regulatory authorities in similar matters.

We have played a key role in many cases that have shaped European competition policy in recent years: from aerospace to software, and manufacturing to transportation. More recently, we have been at the forefront of economic thinking in antitrust investigations and regulation in the tech sector.

We seek candidates for our London, UK location.

Position Overview

The Analyst position is the entry-level position for applicants with an undergraduate qualification in economics. Analysts work closely with senior consultants, scholars and industry experts on project teams, and will have the opportunity to immediately work on some of the largest, high-profile and most significant competition cases in Europe, providing conceptual and practice input to projects. A typical Analyst would:

  • Identify potential issues and conduct analyses that can be used to illustrate economic arguments;
  • Assemble compelling evidence from data and research that support our expert opinions and business recommendations;
  • Program, build models, and/or perform regression analyses in statistical analysis programs (such as Stata, Python, R), including large data projects requiring use of cloud computing;
  • Assist in the development and presentation of client deliverables, including expert reports and white papers summarising opinions, conclusions, and recommendations using financial, market, industry or client-proprietary data;
  • Interact with clients and communicate complicated economic concepts and arguments to non-experts in an understandable, accessible manner;
  • Ensure the integrity and accuracy of analyses and opinions; and
  • Participate in practice-building activities (training, recruiting, publication, expertise sharing, etc.).

Desired Qualifications 

  • An undergraduate qualification (BSc/BA) in economics from well-regarded institutions, graduating between December 2026 and August 2027. The position is ideally suited to candidates considering post-graduate study who would appreciate 1-2 year's employment experience and an insight into the world of economic consulting before returning to university for a postgraduate qualification;
  • Strong foundation in microeconomics, with a specialism in industrial economics preferred;
  • High degree of numeracy and comfort with data manipulation are essential, familiarity with econometric techniques desirable;
  • Curious and analytical thinkers who bring creative approaches to non-standard problems;
  • Effective oral and written communication skills;
  • Eagerness to learn new skills and programming languages;
  • Demonstrated high level of initiative and leadership;
  • Strong teamwork and collaboration capabilities;
  • Excellent time management and task prioritisation skills; and
  • Clear and demonstrated interest in consulting through coursework, work experience, activities, or attendance at CRA recruiting events.

As much of our work occurs in our offices, minimal travel is required.

To Apply

To be considered for this position, please submit the following:

  • CV/Resume – please include current address, personal email and telephone number;
  • Covering letter – please describe your interest in the European Competition practice and how this role matches your goals.
  • Academic Results - please provide all university transcript(s) available to date, including any current or incomplete results.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Career Growth and Benefits 

  • Charles River Associate’s robust skills development programs, including a commitment to offering 100 hours of training annually through formal and informal programs, encourage you to thrive as an individual and team member. Beginning with research and analysis skill building, training continues with technical training, presentation skills, internal seminars, and career mentoring and performance coaching from an assigned senior colleague. Additional leadership and collaboration opportunities exist through internal firm development activities.
  • We offer a comprehensive total rewards program including a superior benefits package, wellness programming to support physical, mental, emotional and financial well-being, and in-house immigration support for foreign nationals and international business travelers.

Work Location Flexibility

Charles River Associates creates a work environment that enables our colleagues to benefit from being together in the office to best deliver on our promise of career growth, mentorship and inclusivity. At the same time, we recognise that individuals realise a range of benefits when working from home periodically. We currently ask that individuals spend 3 to 4 days a week on average working in the office (which may include traveling to another Charles River Associates office or to a client's location), with specific days determined in coordination with your practice or team. At certain times of the year (e.g. holiday periods), additional remote work options are offered to those whose work commitments permit it, although our offices remain open for those who choose or need to be there.

Responsible AI Use in Recruiting

We believe that recruiting is fundamentally a human process, and we are committed to a hiring process that is consistent, transparent, and people-focused. While AI and other technology-enabled tools help our team operate more efficiently, we strive to provide every candidate with a personalized, thoughtful, and high-touch experience. As CRA invests significant human effort to find qualified members for our teams, we expect candidates to invest corresponding human effort to learn about CRA, prepare thoughtful application materials, and engage with our interviewers. Read more about appropriate hiring manager, recruiting team, and candidate AI at CRA on our website.  

Our Commitment to Diversity

Charles River Associates is an Equality Act 2010 employer. As part of our focus on equity and inclusion, we work to ensure a fair and consistent hiring process. We celebrate diversity and we are committed to an inclusive work environment.

The statements included in this job description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of personnel so classified.

job.description: About Niantic Spatial   AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.  That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.  In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.  Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.     About the Role   You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems.  The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves.  You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model.     What You'll Do      Geospatial Registration  — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data.     3D Geometry & Correspondence  — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP.     Data & Evaluation  — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production.     Learning-Based 3D Reasoning  — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling.     Production Robustness  — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps.     Cross-Functional Collaboration  — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems.     Research Communication  — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate.       What You'll Bring     Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience.    Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area.    Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion.    The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously.    Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy).    Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems.    A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data.    Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines.       Nice to Have     PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field — not required, but valued.    A strong publication record or active involvement in the research community at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, 3DV, ICRA, or RSS.    Experience with learning-based approaches for visual or 3D understanding — transformers, point transformers, foundation models, or methods combining learned representations with explicit geometric priors.    Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data.    Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery.       Compensation & Benefits   Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.     Location & Work Model   This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office. We welcome applications from candidates who require visa sponsorship.     Inclusive Application   We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. If you're excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed — you may be exactly who we're looking for.     Equal Opportunity   Niantic Spatial is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment at Niantic Spatial are considered without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions), marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected category under applicable laws. Niantic Spatial will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with applicable laws. Please contact your recruiter if you want to request an accommodation for the job application or interview process.     Candidate Privacy   I understand that by submitting my job application, the information I provide as part of that application will be used in accordance with Niantic Spatial's Privacy Notice for Job Applicants and Candidates  https://www.nianticspatial.com/applicant-privacy-notice . job.description: Company   NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.  Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.  Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.  Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.    Role  The AIT Systems Integration Engineer owns functional and system-level testing of our spacecraft and the verification tracking for each satellite campaign. Working within the Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) team, you will take the satellite from integrated subsystems to a flight-ready, fully verified vehicle.  You will bridge systems engineering, subsystem teams and the AIT Engineering Functions. You will turn requirements into test procedures, run and lead test campaigns, and make sure every requirement is closed out with traceable evidence before launch.   The role suits someone who knows SmallSat development approaches, is hands-on with Hardware and Ground Support Equipment (GSE), and understands how satellite subsystems behave together.    Responsibilities    Functional and system testing    Own the functional and system test programme for the spacecraft, from unit-level acceptance, integration, thought to whole System End-to-End Testing.    Write, review and run test specifications and procedures, including basic functional testing, FDIR, end-to-end tests and mission/day-in-the-life simulations.    Lead test readiness reviews and test review boards, and sign off test reports.    Run tests before, during and after environmental campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMC) to confirm spacecraft health.    Diagnose anomalies, raise and track Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), and drive root-cause investigations with subsystem engineers.    Develop and maintain automated test scripts and telemetry/telecommand (TM/TC) databases used for testing.    Verification tracking    Own the verification matrix (VCRM) for the satellite campaign, mapping each requirement to its method: test, analysis, inspection or review of design.    Plan the verification approach with Systems Engineering and keep it current through the campaign.    Collect and link verification evidence, and report close-out status against milestones.    Prepare verification data packages for key reviews (e.g. CDR, TRR, QR, PSR/FAR) and customer acceptance.    GSE and test infrastructure    Specify, integrate and validate Electrical GSE, including power supplies, battery simulators, RF test sets, umbilicals and break-out boxes.    Maintain the spacecraft checkout software and ground segment interfaces used on the AIT floor.    Make sure GSE is calibrated, configuration-controlled and safe for use with flight hardware.    Integration and campaign support    Support subsystem and payload integration, including electrical interface checks, harness verification and safe-to-mate procedures.    Plan and schedule system test activities within the wider AIT campaign.    Support launch campaign activities, including transport, launch site checkout and launch vehicle interface testing.    Work to cleanroom, ESD and flight hardware handling standards, and contribute to lessons learned for future missions.      Requirements     Degree in Aerospace, Electronic, Electrical or Systems Engineering, Physics, or equivalent experience.    Typically 3+ years in spacecraft AIT, systems integration or test engineering.    Hands-on experience with functional and system-level testing of satellites or space subsystems.    Familiarity with SmallSat development approaches: agile, rapid iteration, protoflight models, and pragmatic use of COTS components.    Working knowledge of satellite subsystems: EPS, OBC/C&DH, ADCS, communications (TT&C and payload RF), propulsion, thermal, structures and payloads.    Experience using and setting up GSE, including EGSE, checkout systems and RF test equipment.    Experience with requirements verification and maintaining a verification matrix through to close-out.    Comfortable with lab equipment: oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, spectrum analysers, logic analysers.    Familiarity with common spacecraft interfaces and protocols (e.g. CAN, I2C, SPI, RS-422, SpaceWire, CCSDS).    Clear technical writing for procedures, test reports and NCRs.      Desirables    End-to-end involvement in at least one satellite mission that reached launch.    Test automation and scripting in Python or similar, and experience with spacecraft control or checkout software (e.g. OpenC3/COSMOS, Yamcs, SCOS-2000).    Experience planning or supporting environmental test campaigns (vibration, TVAC, EMC).    Knowledge of ECSS standards (e.g. ECSS-E-ST-10-02 Verification, ECSS-E-ST-10-03 Testing) or NASA equivalents.    Requirements management tools (e.g. DOORS, Jama, Polarion, Valispace).    Launch campaign experience at a launch site.    Cleanroom and ESD-certified flight hardware handling.    Eligibility for UK security clearance, or the ability to obtain it, if required by the programme.      Personal attributes    Takes ownership: drives tests and verification to close-out without waiting to be asked.    Methodical and detail-focused, with a strong sense of safety and quality around flight hardware.    Calm, structured problem-solver when anomalies appear under schedule pressure.    Communicates clearly across disciplines, from subsystem engineers to programme managers and customers.    Comfortable in a fast-paced SmallSat environment, balancing rigour with pace.    Willing to work flexibly during test and launch campaigns, including occasional travel.       Why NewOrbit Space?      Pioneering space technology  - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.     Ownership and impact  - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.     Equity and competitive salary  - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.     Comprehensive benefits  - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.     Hybrid working  - One dedicated remote day per week.     Visa sponsorship and relocation support  - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.    Find  Jobs in United Kingdom  on Arbeitnow

job.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Engineering teams tackle complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace, building and scaling systems that serve millions of customers, riders and partners every day.

From real-time logistics to resilient infrastructure and marketplace optimisation, we design, build and operate technology that powers Deliveroo’s growth at scale.

We’re looking for a BI Engineer to join our London team. This role is based in our London office with a hybrid setup, typically 3 days in the office.

Get to know our Engineering team — what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect.

 

About the Team

The Core BI team builds and operates the services, integrations and automation that power business intelligence across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt. Our platforms help analysts, Analytics Engineers, Data Scientists, Software Engineers and business teams discover trusted data and make informed decisions at scale.

We combine software engineering, platform ownership, and a strong user focus to make BI tooling reliable, secure, scalable and self-service. The team supports the current BI ecosystem while helping shape a more integrated experience across the DoorDash group.

 

About the Role

job.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

The Anthropic Residency is our paid, fixed-term research program, with placements lasting between six weeks and six months. We are looking for people who have led ambitious work in a variety of technical fields and want to transition to full-time work focused on making sure AI systems are safe and beneficial for all of humanity. If you are a professor in a quantitative discipline, a technical founder or a staff-level engineer and want to transition to work on transformative AI, we want to hear from you. Background in machine learning is not required.

What to expect

  • A concrete, scoped project matched to your background, with direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers
  • Access to Claude models and GPU compute
  • Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community

Interview process

The interview process will include an initial application, recruiter screen, technical assessment, research discussion and a reference check.

Applications for this round close on November 22, 2026 (11:59 PM PT). We expect to make offers in January 2027.

You may be a good fit if you

  • Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole
  • Are excited to transition into working on empirical AI research full-time
  • Have led ambitious work in a variety of technical fields (professor in a quantitative discipline, a technical founder or a staff-level engineer)
  • Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments
  • Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Strong candidates may also

  • Have experience authoring research papers in machine learning, NLP, or AI safety
  • Have experience with LLMs, reinforcement learning or Kubernetes clusters and complex shared codebases

Mentors and research areas

Potential Anthropic mentors include:

  • Sara Price: leads the Alignment Training team; background in data science
  • Ethan Perez: leads the Alignment Science team; background in machine learning
  • Evan Hubinger: leads the Alignment Stress-Testing team; formerly at The Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)
  • Samuel Marks: leads the Scalable Oversight team; background in mathematics
  • Elana Simon: researches the interpretability of language models and biological models; background in biomedical informatics
  • Belinda Li: researches how language models represent the world, users, and themselves; background in natural language processing (PhD, MIT)
  • Jack Lindsey: leads the Model Psychology team; background in theoretical neuroscience
  • Nicholas Carlini: researches adversarial machine learning and AI security; previously at DeepMind and Google Brain
  • Jascha Sohl-Dickstein: works at the intersection of safety and pretraining; background in physics and neuroscience, formerly Principal Scientist at Google Brain

Residents will work on empirical research questions in collaboration with Anthropic's research teams. Areas we are particularly interested in include:

AI safety & alignment

  • Scalable Oversight: Developing techniques to keep highly capable models helpful and honest, even as they surpass human-level intelligence in various domains.
  • Adversarial Robustness and AI Control: Creating methods to ensure advanced AI systems remain safe and harmless in unfamiliar or adversarial scenarios.
  • Model Organisms: Creating model organisms of misalignment to improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise.
  • Model Internals and Interpretability: Advancing our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures.
  • Safeguards Research: Developing robust defenses against adversarial attacks, comprehensive evaluation frameworks for model safety, and automated systems to detect and mitigate potential risks before deployment.
  • AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations.

AI security & frontier red-teaming

  • Stress-testing frontier models to understand the full extent of their current capabilities in fields such as cybersecurity, robotics or cryptography.

ML systems & reinforcement learning

  • Improving how frontier models are trained and building the infrastructure behind that research, from model architecture, optimizers and training data to accelerator simulators, hardware backends and RL environment pipelines.

For a fuller picture of the questions we care about, see our Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions and recent publications from our Alignment, Interpretability and Frontier Red teams.

Logistics

  • Duration: Placements are six weeks, three months or six months, depending on team fit and candidate preferences. Other lengths between three and six months are possible by exception.
  • Location: This application is for a remote UK position, with the option to work from our London office. However, we prefer that Residents work from our San Francisco office, where most of our research staff is based, but remote participation is possible, especially for shorter placements. Most full-time research roles at Anthropic require relocation to San Francisco. Remote participants need to be based in a country where Anthropic can hire.
  • Commitment: Full-time role for the duration of the residency.
  • Compensation: £265,000 to £375,000/year pro-rated for the duration of the residency + benefits
  • Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas for placements of three months or longer. For six-week placements we encourage remote participation from a country where Anthropic can hire.

Applicants may also be considered for the Anthropic Fellows Program.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
£265,000—£375,000 GBP

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

job.description: TLDR: We’re looking for top 1%, high agency, AI-forward engineers to be part of our early team at Resonance in Berlin. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital, to deploy AI into the economy and rebuild businesses for the AI era. You’ll work at the frontier and solve real problems in an environment that champions ownership, autonomy and innovation at pace. Who we are Resonance is an applied AI company. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital. Our mission is to close the AI diffusion gap and rebuild businesses for the AI era. We're looking to hire Europe’s elite AI talent, and we're building our Berlin hub to serve clients across Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Why now We believe the economic diffusion of AI is the major challenge of the next decade. Foundation models are advancing far faster than organisations can absorb them; the bottleneck is embedding AI deeply into the core processes of a company to drive an inflection in pace and create organisational advantage. Europe is falling behind on AI, and we exist to help its businesses build real, defensible advantage from it rather than simply adopting it. The role As an Applied AI Engineer in Berlin, you’ll build the production AI systems behind Resonance’s client engagements across DACH, driving a dramatic acceleration in productivity or a step change in growth for our key clients. You will work at the AI frontier alongside Senior AI Engineers, owning features, integrations and evals end to end. You’ll build and ship agentic systems, from agents and MCP servers into client systems to retrieval and the product around them, working across the stack from data pipelines and the AI layer to the client’s core systems and the interfaces people use. You’ll build evals and observability from day one, take features from first prototype to production, and deploy and extend what we build inside client environments, shipping at pace with the latest AI coding tools. You’ll grow with the firm by contributing to Resonance’s own AI products and shared platform, turning what you learn on each build into reusable components, and taking on more ownership as you grow. What we’re looking for: You have extreme agency and a bias for action, thrive on ambiguity, and are AI-obsessed, getting hands-on with new models and tools the day they hit the market. You typically have up to four years building software at a startup, a scale-up, a fast-moving product team or your own company. You write production Python or TypeScript, have shipped software with an LLM at its core, at work or on your own projects, and have iterated on prompts, agent loops and evals. You’re at home with messy real-world data, APIs and SQL, you ship fast without cutting corners, and you enjoy solving problems with technical and non-technical people. You have consistently been among the top performers in high-performing environments, at university or at work. Forward deployed experience, AI side projects or a company you founded are a plus, and so is German for client work in DACH. What we offer: Competitive total compensation plus equity. Most engineers get one shot at a startup. Here you build many products, not one: our own AI products and platform, and several production AI systems a year across industries. You’ll learn fast alongside people who have embedded AI into 50+ businesses, with scope that grows as fast as your impact. Europe is falling behind on AI, and every build moves another European business to the right side of the productivity chasm. As one of our first engineers in Berlin, you’ll shape how we build, operate and grow. Logistics: Berlin, 3+ days a week in the office or at client sites, mostly in DACH and Europe. English is our working language; German is a plus. We can sponsor visas for eligible candidates, and start dates are flexible. Apply Send your CV, your GitHub profile and a short note on the AI system you're proudest of shipping and the impact it delivered. We hire people from every background and judge them on what they've built. If you don't tick every box, apply anyway. Resonance is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. If you need adjustments at any stage, tell us and we'll make them.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

Compensation: £85,000 - £110,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits | Technology 

About our Engineering Teams:

We have around 650 engineers across Monzo who design and build our in-house banking platform. We have big ambitions for the future, and technology plays a big role in creating a bank our customers want, so engineers at Monzo collaborate across disciplines to solve interesting challenges throughout the company.

These range from the products our customers use everyday to underlying infrastructure, security, payments and finance, customer operations, financial crime, and data, to name just a few areas. As a bank, there is scope for impact across a huge number of opportunities.

How we work 💻

Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. We value meeting in person but we don't have a mandated requirement on office attendance, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs ✨

Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️

Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.

Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life:

At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance.

You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency 🕣✨

If you prefer to work part-time, we'll make this happen whenever we can - whether this is to help you meet other commitments or strike a great work-life balance.

Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼

  • you have strong experience working on the backend of a technology product
  • you want to be involved in building a product that you (and the people you know) use every day
  • you have a product mindset: you care about customer outcomes and you want to make data-informed decisions
  • you’re comfortable working in a team that deals with ambiguity
  • you’re interested in distributed systems and writing resilient software
  • you have some experience with strongly-typed languages (Go, Java, C, Scala etc.).
  • you think you’d enjoy the kind of work we’re doing

At Monzo, we’re dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming team. Drop us your application, we’d love to hear from you!

  • Cassandra for most persistent data storage
  • Kafka for our asynchronous message queue
  • Kubernetes and Docker to schedule and run our services 
  • Envoy Proxy for RPC
  • AWS for most of our production infrastructure and GCP for most of our data infrastructure
  • React for our public web apps and internal tools
  • We also have physical datacenters with actual cables to connect to various third parties

Our interview process involves three main stages: 

  1. Initial Call 
  2. Take home task or pair coding exercise

Our average process takes around 4 weeks but we will always work around your availability.

job.description: About Kernel   Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?    Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.    Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.    Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at  Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout  already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.    We have raised $14M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 5x YoY.     The Role     We have strong product market fit. In 2025 we grew ~5x with world class net dollar retention, mostly from founder-led sales, and now have AEs hitting quota with an emerging playbook.    We're looking for another BDR Manager to accelerate our outbound engine as we scale in 2026. You'll own a team of ~10 BDRs and be responsible for the pipeline that fuels our growth.    You will report to Dave Bentham (Head of Sales) and work closely with our AEs, marketing, and leadership team to make sure the top of funnel is consistently feeding high-quality pipeline.       What You’ll Be Doing    Set the strategy     Work with Dave and the rest of leadership to define ICP, targeting, and outbound messaging.    Translate company targets into clear, measurable BDR goals and ensure pipeline expectations are distributed strategically across the team.    Continuously iterate on outbound plays, channels, and sequences to improve conversion at every stage.    Develop the BDR team to be a talent pool for the rest of the organisation through a culture of constant learning       Set your team     Manage and develop a team of ~10 BDRs across inbound and outbound.    Work alongside our recruiters to grow the team as we scale.    Be accountable for team performance. Coach underperformers, promote top performers, and set a high bar across the board.    Our BDR team is the talent engine for the entire GTM team. Nurturing the best people and helping them be ready for the next role is crucial.       Set the operating cadence     Define qualification criteria and handoff processes that set AEs up to close.    Build repeatable outbound plays that convert, and partner with marketing where needed.    Establish pipeline generation rigor: activity metrics, and predictable output.    Run weekly team reviews, call coaching sessions, and continuous improvement loops.       What You Bring:     4+ years in business development and/or outbound sales, with at least some time managing a BDR or SDR team.    Experience scaling a BDR team (e.g. growing from a handful of reps to 10+) or managing a team of that size.    Strong instincts for messaging, targeting, and what makes outbound actually work.    Comfort operating in ambiguity: you can build process, playbooks, and territory strategy.    Bonus: the deeper your knowledge of RevOps, data, and GTM tools the better.      ⚠️  This role may not be for you if you:     Need lots of structure or polished specs.    You like spending weeks agonizing on a single initiative, or don’t want to rapidly iterate and run experiments.    Require detailed instructions.      ❌  This role is definitely not for you if you:     Prefer remote or hybrid work (requires 4+ days in London office) and/or can’t travel to clients (US+Europe)    Don’t enjoy the pace of an early-stage startup.    Want to carry your own deals instead of building and coaching a team.       What We Offer   We will do our best to offer you the ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.    💰 Salary: £80-120k OTE + equity    🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays    🥕 £450 Monthly Office Dinner Allowance    ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere    🍼 Generous parental leave policy    💼 Pension plan    💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office    🎉 Team events and dinners    🚀 Work directly with the founders to scale the systems that power enterprise AI    🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace      🎫  Visas & Relocation   We can sponsor visas or offer relocation for exceptional candidates. Stage 3 –  Coffee chat with peer, Jack (30min)   Stage 4  – Case study and time on site with Dave & team (1hour).   Final Stage  – Founders interview with CEO, Anders (45min).  If there is mutual fit, we move to references and offer. About Kaluza   Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.  Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.  With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.    What you'll do   You'll own and evolve the technical systems that power P&T Business Operations — Jira architectures, data pipelines, dashboards, and integrations with enterprise platforms. You identify where operational capability could be stronger, scope those opportunities, and design and build solutions in collaboration with the Business Operations Manager. You approach problems with an AI-first mindset and make technical decisions with clarity about trade-offs.    Own and evolve the standardisation of Jira and other Kaluza data systems. Configure, extend, and redesign them to support increasingly complex business operations.    Build and maintain reliable data pipelines and dashboards that turn raw operations data into clear signals for decision-making. Explore where AI agents and autonomous systems can streamline operations. job.description: C++ Software Engineer    Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time      About Us   Reactive Markets is the  2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year  (  Risk.net  ). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.  We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.     The Role   We're looking for a C++ Software Engineer who wants to build low-latency trading infrastructure on Linux. You'll work on the core components of our Switchboard trading platform — pricing engines, connectivity gateways, market-data systems, and the messaging layer that ties them together.  This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall. You build it, you test it, you deploy it, you support it in production, and you improve it. Our engineers own the full lifecycle — from design through to operational excellence. When something breaks at 4pm on a Friday, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.  Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.     What You'll Work On     Modern C++20 and Go on Linux — a modern software stack based on open source    Cloud-native infrastructure on AWS with colocation in key data centres    Microsecond-level latency optimisation and high-throughput messaging    Market-data and reference-data pipelines across multiple asset classes    FIX protocol integrations with global banks and liquidity providers    Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make system behaviour visible    Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional       What We Need    Technical:     Strong C++ with Linux systems programming (3+ years)    Comfortable working close to the metal — you understand what's underneath your code    Experience with performance-sensitive systems (profiling, optimisation, deterministic behaviour)    Familiarity with networking fundamentals (TCP/UDP, socket programming)    Go experience is a strong bonus — we use Go extensively for microservices and command-line tooling, and you'll be expected to work with it internally. If you don't know it yet, strong C++ engineers pick it up quickly    Python for scripting, automation, testing, and data analysis — used across the platform for tooling and operational workflows    Git and shell scripting    Experience in financial services or trading technology is a plus but not essential     How you work:      You ship.  You're delivery-focused — you iterate, you improve, you get things into production     You own it.  When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You respond to incidents (15-minute acknowledgement SLA during working hours), investigate issues, and close the loop     You write things down.  Documentation is not an afterthought — it's how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist     You communicate.  We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication — especially when things go wrong — is essential     You care about quality.  You write clean, testable code. You review your peers' work thoughtfully. You push for continuous improvement without gold-plating     You embrace AI tooling.  We use AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to amplify our engineering capability — from code review and debugging to incident investigation and documentation. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to learn       What You Get      Real problems  —   trading systems where performance is measured in microseconds, not user clicks     An excellent team  — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards     Ownership  — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients     Competitive package  — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites     Remote-friendly  — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver     Sustainable pace  — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp     Growth  — career progression to senior roles, performance specialisation, or technical leadership. We invest in people who invest in us    We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.  We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.     Our Hiring Process   We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.   Stage 1: Initial Conversation  with Talent Acquisition Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes   Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation  with the relevant team lead or hiring manager Format: Video call, ~60 minutes   Stage 3: Technical Interview  with two members of the relevant engineering team Format: Video call, interactive session, ~60 minutes  What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.  *Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around. Support the preparation of training material for new and existing users. Support users and create documentation based on frequent support requests    Work with engineering, PLM, CAD, and IT colleagues to improve data quality and user experience.      What we're looking for    Required    Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's programme in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.    Good communication skills in English.    Basic experience with Siemens NX and strong interest in CAD, engineering data management, PLM, or technical systems administration.    Organised, detail-oriented, and comfortable working with structured data and technical information.    A proactive, hands-on attitude and willingness to learn.    Comfortable working collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.    Nice to have    Basic familiarity with PLM concepts or systems such as Siemens Teamcenter.    Experience with C# and .Net, Powershell    Basic understanding of engineering drawing standards, part numbering, metadata, or configuration management.    Some exposure to Linux, IT infrastructure, databases, or technical support processes.    Interest in aerospace, spacecraft, or other complex technical environments.       Why you should join us! job.description: About us   At STRATOS Technologies, we are transforming how companies make data-driven decisions. Our software integrates complex datasets into a unified solution, enabling businesses to strengthen their long-term strategies through clear and actionable insights.  Our founders, former business and tech executives who led a $1B division at a Fortune 500 industrial company, originally built a digital twin of their enterprise to drive synchronized planning and execution. Seeing the market’s lack of such a system, they launched STRATOS in 2022 with a bold mission: to unifiy all internal and external data into a single platform.  Today, STRATOS is a category-defining, rapidly growing startup funded extensively by high-profile investors (e.g., Accel) and trusted by nearly a dozen global industrial leaders and Fortune 500 customers. Our software integrates complex datasets into a unified solution, combining deep data integration, best-in-class workflows, and cutting-edge generative AI.  From commercial AI agents to embedded intelligence that supercharges lean teams, STRATOS enables businesses to achieve 10x productivity and strengthen long-term strategies through actionable insights. We are now expanding our team to accelerate our growth even further and help our customers outperform their competition   The role.  You own a piece of the relationship with one of our customers: their data, their questions, and whether the product answers them. You will do the analysis, present it to their commercial leadership, and take what you learn back to our engineers as something we should build. The difference from where you are now is that you stay with it. You see whether the recommendation worked, and when it doesn't, you're the one who fixes it.   The roles you'll play      Owner of a workstream  — take a defined part of the deployment end to end: the market model, the target list or the scoring logic, from first data through to something the customer's teams use every week.       Advisor to the customer's commercial team  — run working sessions with sales and commercial leadership, present your own analysis, and handle the challenge yourself. You are in the room, not behind it.       Co-owner of the account  — you share the relationship with a senior CPM and take on more of it as the year goes on, up to running a customer of your own.       Voice of the customer in our roadmap  — turn what you see in the field into what we build, and stay with it through the roadmap until it ships.       Builder of how we work  — sharpen the standards, templates and tooling that make the next deployment better than the last.     Who this is for.  Most people who do well here have one to three years behind them in strategy consulting, corporate strategy, or an analytical commercial role.    You have run a workstream yourself: not just the analysis, but the stakeholder who didn't want to give you the data and the deadline that moved.      You are quick in data and you check your own numbers. Excel and PowerPoint are assumed; any SQL or Python is a bonus, not a requirement, and we'll teach you what you need.      You can present to people twenty years your senior without either deferring to them or lecturing them.      You are curious about how industrial businesses actually work — how a building-materials group reaches its customers, why a distributor behaves the way it does.      You want more responsibility than your peers get, and you understand that comes with being the one who is wrong in public sometimes.     This probably isn't for you if you want to specialise early, or if you'd rather be handed a defined analysis than decide what the right question is.    What we offer     Equity through our stock option programme, so you share in the long-term success and growth of the company      A highly competitive salary      Direct access to Fortune 500 executives from your first months, at a level most people wait a decade for      Work alongside former MBB consultants and Fortune 500 executives who will teach you directly — our team is small enough that this happens in person, not through a training curriculum      Private healthcare      Pension scheme      25 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays      Work from abroad — up to four weeks a year, and up to two weeks at a time      Hybrid office policy, with visa sponsorship available      A company committed to social and environmental responsibility — we pledge to be a net-zero CO₂ company and donate 1% of our revenue to social causes     Practicalities     London-based, 3 days a week in our Farringdon office      Travel to some customer sites around, mostly within Europe      German is genuinely useful here and several of our customers are German-speaking, but it is not a requirement     The process     First round with our Talent Lead — 30 minutes      Tehcncial case interview — 45 minutes      Hiring manager interview with a senior executive - 30 minutes      Second senior executive interview, which may include a case exercise - 30 minutes      Final stage with our CEO - 45 minutes    Questions before applying:  Find more  English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom  on Arbeitnow

job.description: Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future.  Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. Strong background in numerical methods for ODEs and PDEs: discretisation, stiff and implicit solvers, nonlinear and sparse linear solvers. Plasma, fluid, electromagnetic, or other multiphysics simulation.    Having led the design of a scientific codebase used by others. job.description: About Plasma   Plasma is building the primary account for global money.  Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders.  Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.  Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.  Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.  The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.      The Team &    Our Story    We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.  We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.        Customer Experience     Plasma is scaling its customer-facing operations across international markets, and we’re growing the Customer Experience Team to match. You’ll join an established team and take ownership of coverage for the CET time zone, making sure our customers get great support when they need it most.  You’ll work across the full customer journey, from first contact through to resolution. Because we’re still building out our playbook, your input will directly shape the processes, standards, and team culture as we grow. You won’t just follow the process; you’ll help refine it.  Some flexibility in working hours & weekend shifts will be needed to support coverage and the occasional busy period. We’re looking for a hard-working self-starter who thrives in a fast-moving startup environment and is committed to the mission alongside the rest of the team.        The role       Own the customer experience day-to-day:  Be the first person our customers reach when something goes wrong or they need help. You will handle inbound queries across chat, email, and support tooling, and take accountability for the quality and speed of every response.     Be the right hand of the Ops lead:  Work directly alongside the Head of Operations to build out processes, identify gaps, and support decisions as we scale the team internationally. This is not a back-office support role. You will be involved in how we think about operations.     Build the foundations:  We are early. Many of the processes, templates, and escalation paths do not exist yet. You will create them. From response frameworks to internal guides, you will help lay the groundwork the team will rely on as we grow.     Support international team scaling:  As we hire Ops team members in new markets, you will help onboard them, share knowledge, and maintain consistency in how we deliver for customers across regions.     Spot problems before they become patterns:  Track issues across the customer base, flag recurring themes to Product and Engineering, and help prioritise fixes that actually move the needle for customers.     Work across teams:  Collaborate with Compliance, KYC, and Product to make sure the customer experience is joined up, especially during onboarding and verification flows where things can go wrong quickly.     Represent the customer internally:  Your proximity to customer feedback is valuable. Use it. Bring customer insight into internal conversations and push for improvements that matter.     Be Flexible with Shift Rotation:  Most weeks you’ll work the normal Mon-Fri, however team members currently rotate weekend shifts which means that you may be required to work a weekend shift once every 6 weeks. You’ll then be able to take those days worked off the following week.        The Bar       1 to 3 years of experience  in customer operations, customer success, or a support role, ideally within fintech, payments, or crypto. We will consider strong candidates from outside these sectors if the fit is right.     Someone who takes ownership.  You do not wait to be told. When something is broken or missing, you fix it or flag it. You hold yourself to a high standard even when no one is watching.     Clear and direct in how you communicate.  You can write a helpful, professional response under pressure and explain a complex situation simply. You know the difference between being thorough and overcomplicating things.     Competent English Language  - our team communicates in english so being competent with the language is a requirement.     Comfortable with ambiguity.  This is an early-stage company. Processes will change, priorities will shift, and some days you will be figuring things out as you go. You see that as interesting rather than frustrating. Preferably, you have worked at a fast-paced tech company.     Genuinely curious about crypto.  You do not need deep technical knowledge, but you need to understand the basics of how stablecoins and digital assets work and be motivated to learn more. Our customers live in this space.     Organised under pressure.  You can manage a queue, prioritise effectively, and keep quality high when things are busy.     Collaborative by default.  You work well with people in different functions, different time zones, and different levels of seniority. Building the team abroad means working with people you may never meet in person, and you are good at that.        Nice to have       Experience in a startup or scale-up  where you had to build or rebuild processes, not just follow them.     Exposure to Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk , or similar support tooling in a live production environment.     Any familiarity with KYC or compliance workflows  as they relate to customer onboarding.     Experience supporting or managing a small team , even informally, or helping onboard new colleagues.     An interest in how stablecoin and DeFi products work  and the customer challenges they create.     Multilingual skills  that could support customer communication across our international markets.       What's in it for you     Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.    A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.    Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.    Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.    All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.    Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day. 🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us. 

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

 

📍London or UK remote | 💰 £100,000 to £130,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits | Technology - Data  

 

⭐ About Data at Monzo

Data is at the heart of how we make decisions and build products at Monzo. Our Data teams bring together Data Science, Analytics Engineering, Data Analytics and Machine Learning, working closely with Product, Engineering and other teams across the business.

Our Data Scientists are embedded within product and business areas across Monzo, where they use experimentation, causal inference, statistical modelling, machine learning and analytics to understand our customers, identify opportunities and influence the direction of our products and strategy.

As a Data Science Manager, you'll lead a team of Data Scientists and other Data professionals within one of these areas, combining people leadership with strategic data leadership and close partnership with senior stakeholders.

🔑 You'll play a key role by...

You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering and senior leaders to ensure data plays a central role in how we understand problems, make decisions and develop our products.

You'll lead and develop a team of talented Data Scientists, helping them do their best work while setting a high bar for analytical quality and impact. You'll provide strategic direction across complex problems, help teams identify where Data Science can have the greatest impact, and ensure insights translate into meaningful decisions and product changes.

We have a strong culture of data-driven decision making across Monzo. We're big believers in powerful, accessible analytics and empowering teams across the business to answer questions themselves. Around 90% of our day-to-day data-driven decisions are supported by self-serve analytics through Looker, giving our Data teams the space to focus on higher-impact problems.

Your day-to-day

  • Lead, develop and grow a team of exceptional Data Scientists and other Data professionals.
  • Hire, coach and retain talented people while creating an environment where they can develop and do their best work.
  • Set the Data Science direction for your area and identify where data can have the greatest customer and business impact.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering and senior stakeholders to shape strategy and influence product direction.
  • Bring analytical rigour to complex and ambiguous problems and help teams turn them into clear, actionable opportunities.
  • Ensure teams are using the right analytical approaches, from experimentation and causal inference through to statistical modelling and machine learning.
  • Help connect Data Science work to measurable customer, product and commercial outcomes.
  • Work with Analytics Engineering, Machine Learning and other Data disciplines to ensure teams have the data, tooling and infrastructure they need.
  • Contribute to the wider Data Science discipline at Monzo, helping us continually raise the bar for how we work.

🤩 We'd love to hear from you if...

  • What we're doing at Monzo excites you!
  • You have significant experience managing and developing Data Scientists.
  • You're a strong strategic data leader who uses data to influence decisions and direction.
  • You have experience partnering with senior and executive stakeholders across different functions and levels of seniority.
  • You're comfortable working autonomously in a fast-growing and evolving organisation.
  • You have a strong understanding of Data Science approaches including experimentation, causal inference, statistical analysis and machine learning.
  • You're comfortable with tools and languages such as Python and SQL, and understand how to choose the right analytical approach for a problem.
  • You can build credibility with Product, Engineering and senior business leaders and influence without relying on authority.
  • You have strong product judgement and experience using Data Science to shape product development and strategy.
  • You know how to balance technical excellence with pragmatic decision-making and business impact.
  • You have experience helping Data Scientists develop their technical, product and leadership capabilities.

The interview process

Our interview process involves 3 main stages. We promise not to ask you any brain teasers or trick questions!

  • 30-minute recruiter call
  • 45-minute call with the hiring manager
  • 3 x 1-hour video calls with various team members

Our average process takes around 3–4 weeks, but we'll always work around your availability. You'll have the chance to speak to our recruitment team at various points during the process.

What's in it for you

✈️ We can help you relocate to the UK

✅ We can sponsor visas

📍 This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK, with ad hoc meetings in London.

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team.

📚 Learning budget of £1,000 a year for books, training courses and conferences

➕And much more, see our full list of benefits here

We're looking for a sharp, analytical data scientist to own the evaluation and quality loop of our AutoQA product. You can be early in your career (recent graduates with strong LLM fundamentals are welcome), we have room and a clear path for you to grow.    In a nutshell    Join a fast-growing SaaS company in an international environment (steep learning curve guaranteed).    Own a high-impact problem: making LLM-powered quality assurance measurably accurate at scale.    Sit at the intersection of AI and CX, working directly with enterprise customers and their real-world QA rubrics.    Grow into a Senior Data Scientist, AI Engineer, or ML Engineer role. We invest in progression.    Enjoy the perks: flexible hours, open holiday policy, an office in the heart of Amsterdam with hybrid flexibility, visa sponsorship, great gear, workations, and team events.      About Kaizo  At Kaizo, we build a performance development and quality platform for customer support teams. Our AutoQA product uses LLMs to review support conversations against each customer's own quality rubric, automatically and at scale. Behind it sits a microservices-based stream processing platform handling over 200 million events per day (Kafka, Kubernetes on Google Cloud, ElasticSearch, MongoDB, BigQuery), and an LLMOps stack built around LangSmith for experimentation, prompt management, and tracing.  The hard part isn't calling an LLM. It's knowing, with evidence, how well the system performs on every customer's unique rubric, and having a reliable, repeatable way to improve it. That's where you come in.    What you'll focus on       Translate customer rubrics into AutoQA instructions.  Work with real customer quality criteria and turn them into precise, testable instructions that LLMs can score reliably.     Run experiments that move accuracy.  Design and execute evaluation experiments on large, representative datasets using LangSmith and BigQuery, and track quality with our performance metrics.     Build the datasets that make evaluation possible.  Curate raw production data into golden datasets with balanced coverage, and generate synthetic data to cover the rare cases that matter most. QA is a discipline of rare occurrences: distributions are skewed, positives are scarce, and resourcefulness beats volume.     Build LLM-as-a-judge pipelines  to assess system quality internally and make evaluation repeatable.     Make results actionable.  Your experiments should end in a decision: change a prompt, adjust which tools the system uses, surface context the AI is missing, or flag where new capabilities are needed. You'll work with the AI team to ship those decisions.     Evaluate across the full stack.  Beyond scoring quality, you'll help validate retrieval (RAG/IR), tool calling, and speech pipelines (transcription and diarization quality).     Join customer calls with the team  to understand how QA leaders define quality, and feed what you learn back into the product.      What you'll grow into    Shaping how customers monitor quality themselves, catch drift, and keep their AutoQA setup improving over time.    Smarter categorization and routing of conversations to power analytics and get the right tickets to the right evaluation.             A solid understanding of how LLMs work and hands-on experience prompting them for accuracy (coursework, thesis, internships, or side projects all count; production experience is a bonus).    Good applied statistics: experiment design, classifier evaluation, precision/recall trade-offs, and working with heavily imbalanced data.    Strong Python skills and fluency with the standard data toolkit (Pandas, NumPy, Jupyter). SQL is a plus.    An analytical, evidence-first mindset: you'd rather measure than assume.    Product sense and empathy for end users. You'll be building for QA managers and support agents, not just for benchmarks.    Excellent written and verbal communication. You'll present findings to the team and join customer conversations.    0 to 2 years of industry experience. Recent graduates with strong relevant work are encouraged to apply.    A team player who's comfortable wearing multiple hats. We're an early-stage company and things move fast.     Bonus points for:     Experience with LangSmith or similar LLMOps/evaluation tooling    Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, Docker, or Kubernetes    Speech/audio processing or ASR evaluation    Fine-tuning or building synthetic datasets for LLMs      Who you'll work with    You'll join our AI team (two data scientists, an AI engineer, and an ML engineer) and collaborate closely with our data engineers, frontend engineers, designer, product manager, and CX teams. You'll have mentorship from day one and real ownership fast.    What's in it for you? We help companies automate the most critical parts of finance, from closing the books and recognizing revenue to consolidating entities and reporting to investors. Partner with internal teams across Product, Engineering, and Customer Success
