job.description: TL;DR  You know how to walk into an enterprise, spot the pain points in its ERP processes, and see what good could look like. At Conduct you turn that into a game changing moment: you show leadership, with confidence, how Conduct will transform the way they run SAP. You own optimising the delivery of transformation projects with Conduct, from the first use case to adoption across the business. You build the trust that turns a pilot into a long-term partnership, and the product insights you bring back directly shape what we build next.   Why Conduct  The world's largest companies should move at the speed of their ideas, not the speed of the systems they run on. Today they don't, and you've seen why firsthand.  Every new product line, pricing change or process redesign runs into SAP estates layered with decades of custom code, user exits and enhancements no single person fully understands. Requirements take months to ship. S/4HANA migrations cost $100M+ and years of pain, and the 2027 ECC deadline is forcing every large enterprise to face it.  We're building the AI operating system that absorbs this complexity and gives enterprises back their speed. Major enterprises already trust us with their most critical systems. We've closed game-changing SI partnerships, just raised a $60M Series A, and demand is outpacing what we can service.  We're a small, talent-dense team doing our life's work out of London and NYC. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here shapes the company and how the world's largest companies operate. We sponsor visas and are convinced diverse teams build better products, so we especially encourage underrepresented groups in tech to reach out.   What you'll own  You will make sure Conduct lands and sticks inside our most strategic SAP customers. You join accounts early, shape how Conduct fits into their transformation programmes, and fully take over post-sale. You'll have a direct line from what you see in the field to what ships in the product.     Be the SAP brain in the room.  Translate between CIOs, process owners, Basis teams and our engineers. Scope use cases across finance, supply chain, procurement and sales that land real value fast.     Design the transformation.  Get under the skin of complex, heavily customised ECC and S/4HANA landscapes. Conceptualise where Conduct can have the biggest impact, then lead the deployment that gets the customer there.     Turn pilots into partnerships.  Onboard hundreds of end users, prove ROI, spot expansion signals and hold the early commercial conversations that grow an account.     Shape the product.  You'll have a direct line into product and engineering. Your view of how SAP actually runs in the real world will shape our roadmap.     Build the engine.  Our GTM team is small and lean. You'll build the onboarding flows, tooling and reusable playbooks that let customer capacity compound without headcount growing linearly.     Work with our SI partners.  You speak their language. Help partners deploy Conduct inside their own programmes.    No two days look the same. You'll fly out to customers when it counts and spend the rest of the time building alongside the team.   Who we hire  We're looking for people obsessed with delivering for customers. You'll fit right in if former colleagues would, without hesitating, call you one of the sharpest people they've worked with.  In practice that tends to look like:     3+ years in SAP or ERP consulting , at a Big Four firm, a global SI or a specialist SAP partner. You've been on live implementations, rollouts or S/4HANA transformations, not just advisory.     Real depth in at least one area of SAP.  Functional (FI/CO, SD, MM, PP, EWM), technical (ABAP, integration, BTP) or solution architecture. You understand how processes and custom code fit together across the landscape.     Client-facing confidence.  You've run workshops, owned a workstream and earned the trust of senior stakeholders who were sceptical at first.     Commercial instinct.  You notice the next problem worth solving, and you understand that a great deployment is how accounts grow.     Builder energy.  You want to do the hands-on customer work and build the process behind it. Ambiguity excites you more than it worries you.     Curiosity about AI.  You don't need to be an engineer. You do need to want to learn how it works and where it breaks.     Low ego, high self-awareness.  You're comfortable saying "I don't know" in a complex technical room, then going and figuring it out.    Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We care more about trajectory and sharpness than a perfect match.  Find more  English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom  on Arbeitnow

job.description:
In a nutshell

Join us in designing the future of grocery shopping. As a Product Designer in our consumer team, you'll own the design of our core mobile app, shaping the daily shopping experience for hundreds of thousands of people in The Netherlands, Germany and France. You'll tackle the unique challenge of designing for a task that is frequent, personal, and central to our customers' lives. You'll be part of a dedicated product team and our wider UX Guild, a creative community that ensures a world-class user experience across Picnic. We’re looking for a passionate designer to join our Amsterdam HQ and help build a product people genuinely love, in a fast-scaling environment that values autonomy, collaboration, and adaptability over rigid processes.

Tricks of the trade

  • Have the autonomy to own the design of new features from beginning to end. Everything you do matters and will be developed and tested at a fast pace.
  • Sharpen project briefs based on explorative research together with UX researchers and product owners. 
  • Build low and high fidelity prototypes to be tested and evaluated on a weekly basis with real users.
  • Document the final design requirements on interaction and UI level to brief and support developers during the development phase. 
  • Learn and grow through the continuous feedback and mentoring by seasoned UX designers and researchers. 
  • Support the development and maintenance of our design libraries and system.
  • Continuously explore new ideas in order to initiate new projects and improvements, design is never done ;). 

Your superpowers

  • You have a completed degree in a relevant design field (e.g. CMD, UX, Interaction or Product Design)
  • You have 0-3 years of experience as a UX designer and have worked on or have a strong interest in building great products
  • Your portfolio has user-centered design cases that show your problem solving capabilities
  • You have a deep curiosity to understand our customers and have hands-on experience in exploratory research to discover and define user problems from scratch
  • You know your way around Figma and are able to craft high-fidelity designs that fit into our design system
  • You bring a low-ego, collaborative mindset and enjoy building solutions together

job.description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity.  We want you as a talented intern to help us in our mission by contributing to the development, justification and validation of our Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS).    As an ECLSS engineer intern, you will ensure that the system undergoes the correct steps to qualify it for flight. This inter-disciplinary position includes hands-on work on the test benches for the Pressure Control System (PCS), the Air Recirculation System (ARS) and the Crew and Emergency systems (CES). A major part of the work is to ensure the activities are documented properly according to the ECSS development process.    Key responsibilities  In your position as an ECLSS Engineer Intern, your role includes:    Verifying NASA ISS requirements applicable to ECLSS components through test and analysis data.    Build hands-on on test support equipments (GSEs) and functional test benches.    Supporting test activities and validating simulation results against test data for accuracy and reliability    Qualifying hardware components for internal designs and externally sourced parts in environmental testing such as vibration, shock and thermal cycling    Communicating effectively and providing recommendations through the preparation and presentation of technical data    Writing technical documentation and participating in internal and external reviews       What we would love to see from you    Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Engineering Science, or Mechanical Engineering    Hands-on experience with aerospace hardware, ideally pressure systems    Strong background in fluid mechanics    Experience with programming (Python) and data analysis    Ability to work both independently and as part of a team    Precision in ensuring compliance with ECSS processes    Understanding the implications of interacting with a crewed space station    Systems engineering mindset    Fluent in English; German is a plus    Strong skills in organizing and prioritizing of tasks    Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done    Ability to communicate across all levels of the organization    Behavior consistent with The Exploration Company's core values: Commitment, Innovation, Trust, Quality, and Teamwork       Why you should join us!   What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:      We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind     We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them      We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?      We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. job.description:
Joining Capco means joining an organization that is committed to an inclusive working environment where you’re encouraged to #BeYourselfAtWork. We celebrate individuality and recognize that diversity and inclusion, in all forms, is critical to success. It’s important to us that we recruit and develop as diverse a range of talent as we can and we believe that everyone brings something different to the table – so we’d love to know what makes you different. Such differences may mean we need to make changes to our process to allow you the best possible platform to succeed, and we are happy to cater to any reasonable adjustments you may require. You will find the section to let us know of these at the bottom of your application form or you can mention it directly to your recruiter at any stage and they will be happy to help.

About Capco

Capco is a global technology and management consultancy dedicated to the financial services industry. We combine innovative thinking with unrivalled industry knowledge, to offer our clients consulting expertise, complex technology and package integration, transformation delivery and managed services to move their organizations forward.

  • We specialize primarily in banking & payments, capital markets, wealth & asset management, insurance and energy
  • We have a collaborative and efficient approach
  • We help our clients successfully innovate, increase revenue, manage risk and regulatory change, reduce costs and enhance controls
  • We serve our clients from 32 offices across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific

If creativity and innovation are your passion, then Capco is right for you. You can grow in an inclusive, diverse and collaborative environment. At Capco, we will train and support you to help accelerate your career. 

 

The Role

As a Finance Data Engineer at Capco, you will work at the intersection of IT, Data and Finance, supporting the evolution of a critical Finance Data Mart used for Business Finance information, MI and reporting in Private Banking as well as other Banking areas. 

The platform is a key source of financial information, supporting measures including such as Assets under Management (AuM), Net New Money (NNM) and Return on Assets (RoA) and other KPIs.  

You will combine technical and data expertise with Finance understanding, enabling you to interpret and validate financial outputs, identify issues and help improve the quality and capabilities of the platform.

Your code will interface directly with vehicle avionics, guidance systems, propulsion, communications, and ground control. The position level will be determined based on your experience, technical depth, and ability to take ownership. Key Responsibilities Design, implement, and own core flight software modules for spacecraft control, telemetry, data handling, fault management, and communications. Develop in modern C++ and Python for support tooling, following best practices in software architecture, testing, and performance optimization. Build and maintain test frameworks for automated unit, integration, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing to validate software behavior across mission phases. Create and run high-fidelity simulations to model flight dynamics, subsystem interactions, and edge cases. Collaborate closely with GNC, avionics, propulsion, and mission operations teams to ensure seamless integration and mission success. Good understanding of communication protocols such as: TCP/IP, UART, CAN Bus and serialization. Experience with automotive or flight software frameworks. Background in orbital mechanics, spacecraft systems, or space mission lifecycle. Experience with industry standards such as AUTOSAR, ECSS, DO-178. Why you should join us! Forward Deployed Engineer

About HSO

HSO is a global Business Transformation Partner with deep industry expertise and a long standing strategic relationship with Microsoft. We help organisations unlock the full potential of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Azure, Data and AI technologies to modernise operations, accelerate innovation and deliver meaningful business outcomes.

In 2026, HSO achieved Microsoft Frontier Partner status, recognising our advanced capabilities across Microsoft Cloud and AI and our ability to help customers move beyond AI experimentation into secure, governed, enterprise scale production.

With operations across Europe, North America and Asia, we combine industry knowledge, technical excellence and a practical, people first approach to transformation.

As we continue to expand our AI capabilities, we’re building a new generation of customer facing engineering talent to help organisations turn the potential of AI and agentic technologies into real, measurable value.

About the Role

HSO is building a new generation of customer facing engineers who will help our customers create the operating model of the future using the latest AI, data and cloud capabilities.

Forward Deployed Engineers combine consulting judgement, production software engineering, data platform expertise, AI delivery capability and business transformation skills.

You will embed with strategic customers, understand their most important business challenges and rapidly turn those challenges into working, production ready AI applications, agentic workflows, automation solutions and data driven platforms.

This is a hands on, outcome led role embedded within customer environments. You’ll move quickly from discovery to working software and take accountability for delivering measurable business outcomes.

You’ll work across business processes, data platforms, integrations, AI, cloud and security, designing solutions that make effective use of Microsoft technologies while integrating with the customer’s wider technology estate.

A strong understanding of modern enterprise data platforms is fundamental to the role. You will need to understand how data is structured, governed, integrated, transformed and made available to AI and application workloads, and how data platform decisions affect the quality, scalability and reliability of the solutions you build.

Forward Deployed Engineers work closely with Deployment Strategists. The Deployment Strategist focuses on identifying where AI can create the greatest customer value and defining the desired outcome. The FDE takes ownership of how that outcome is delivered technically.

From discovery through to go live, both roles work side by side. The FDE owns the technical solution and delivery, while the Deployment Strategist ensures the solution remains aligned to the business problem and measurable value.

We're looking for Junior Forward Deployed Engineers to join the team and:    Deploy our existing product offering to new and existing customers. job.description:
About Moneybox  
   
  At Moneybox, our mission is to give everyone the means to get more out of life. We're guided by our belief that wealth isn't about the money, it's about the means to more - more freedom, opportunities, possibilities, and peace of mind. Moneybox is an award-winning wealth management platform, helping over one and a half million people build wealth throughout their lives, whether they’re saving and investing, buying their first home, or planning for retirement.  
   
   Job Brief       
 Moneybox serves more than 2M customers and runs a live service handling over 20M API requests a day. We have agreed a company-wide AI Platforms strategy and are building a new AI Deployment team to deliver on it. This is the first of several Senior AI Deployment Engineer hires, reporting to the Head of AI Platforms & Deployment. 
 You will be a forward-deployed senior engineer who unlocks AI-driven solutions to business problems: an expert in  deploying  AI and using it safely, not an ML modeller. The work is mainly Python across the modern AI engineering stack - harness engineering, skills and tool building, agent workflows and orchestration, agent hosting and sandboxing, guardrails, evals, RAG and context engineering, and tokenomics (cost, latency, model selection). Production-grade LLM system experience is the core requirement. 
 You will work on three types of project: 
 
  Departmental engagements.  Embed with departments to AI-enable tasks and processes in a more sophisticated way than "just ask Claude" - for example, Python pipelines where one step is an LLM API call - delivering real incremental value with each engagement and transforming working patterns into load-bearing, AI-enabled business processes. 
  Customer-facing AI deployment.  Deploy and integrate AI components built by our ML and Decisioning teams into production: the engineering implementation layer between a working model and a live customer feature. 
  AI platform capabilities.  Work with the AI Platforms team to turn engagement patterns into safe, increasingly self-serve company-wide tooling. 
 
 Departments across Moneybox are already building AI tools themselves - we want to provide them with a safe path to load-bearing use at scale. This role catches that demand and matures it properly. 
   What You'll Do   

  Own engagement delivery end to end.  Scope with the department, design the solution, build it, deploy it, and agree the handover and ownership model - from prototype through to stable production. Engagements arrive as vague pain; you define the problem, not just the solution. 
  Engineer AI solutions properly.  Pipelines, LLM API integration, evals, guardrails, monitoring, and cost and accuracy optimisation for the systems you build. Know when a step must be deterministic and when an LLM is the right tool. 
  Graduate tools into business systems.  Take shared, team-load-bearing tools that people have built for themselves and rebuild them as owned business

job.description: About Seamflow   Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files.  Where we are:    Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry    $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed, co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze.    Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists.     The team   Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further.   The role   A Front End Design Engineer thinks in finished interfaces, not mockups or components in isolation. A technical reviewer at a notified body spends their day inside a 400-page technical file, cross-referencing clauses, checking test reports against standards, and deciding whether a medical device is safe to sell. Today they do that in Word, Acrobat and a spreadsheet someone built in 2011. The interface they use decides how fast they work and whether they trust the AI sitting next to them.  You own that interface. Layout, typography, interaction, motion, the design system underneath it, and the React that ships it. You decide how a reviewer sees a finding, how they correct a model that got it wrong, and how a hundred fields of dense regulatory data become something a person can actually read. You sketch it, build it, ship it, then sit next to someone using it and find out what you got wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week.   What we're looking for   We care far more about taste and engineering strength than about matching a list of tools. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in React, Svelte, Vue or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, craft and speed are not.  What we're actually screening for:    You've designed and built an interface that real people used every day. Not a Dribbble shot, not a component library nobody adopted. Something that shipped, got used, and got better.    You have taste, and you can defend it. Typography, spacing, motion, hierarchy. You notice when something is a few pixels off and you can explain why it matters.    You build the whole thing. Design, frontend, the state and data it sits on. You don't hand the code to someone else once the Figma is done, and you don't hand the design to someone else once the code is.    You can design for density. Expert users, complex workflows, hundreds of fields on a screen. Making that clear is much harder than making a landing page beautiful.    You go to the source. You'll watch a technical reviewer work through a real file, and you'll design for what they actually do rather than what the process diagram says.    Signals we like, none of them required:  design engineering or front-end roles at somewhere like Linear, Vercel, Notion or Figma, a design system you built and maintained, work on interfaces where people review or correct AI output, founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup.   This is probably not for you if     You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch.    You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning.    You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane.     What you get     Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar    Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room    Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly    Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster    A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics    If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV.  Find more  English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom  on Arbeitnow

job.description: Our Mission:  Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.  Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.  Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.  Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.    Find out more about the team and life at Omnea  here .     What We're Looking For   We're looking for a  Frontend Lead Engineer  to own the front end at Omnea.  Our design system is growing fast, our front-end architecture is becoming more complex, and right now ownership of these things is distributed. You'd be the person who takes this to the next level.  You'll work across every product team. You'll own the design system, own the front-end architecture, and set the standard for how we build interfaces. We're a tight-knit group of ambitious builders who hold the bar high. It took over 10,000 interviews to hire our first 50 Omneans. Over the next year, our engineering team will double in size, our enterprise customer base will grow from ~180 to 300+, and revenue will triple. The front end has to scale with it.  This is a craft role with real leverage. Almost every engineer at Omnea ships front end. What you build determines how well they do it.  Procurement is a harder interface problem than it sounds. Approval workflows that branch and re-route, dense tables people live in all day, intake forms that adapt to what someone is buying. Getting this right is the difference between software people tolerate and software people actually like using.     What Can You Expect On Our Engineering Team?      Join a Skilled Team.  Become part of one of Europe's fastest-growing software companies, working alongside experienced full-stack product engineers and product designers from top technology businesses and startups.     Own the Design System.  You'll own our design system outright: components, patterns, tokens, documentation, and adoption. You'll partner closely with Design to turn intent into reusable, high-quality primitives.     Own the Front-End Architecture.  Deployment strategy, performance, build tooling, and the conventions everyone else follows. You'll set the direction rather than inherit it, working alongside the engineers and designers closest to each surface rather than owning it in isolation.     Leverage Across Every Team.  You'll work with all of our engineering teams on their most front-end-heavy projects. The work you do multiplies across the whole org.     A Real Design Partnership.  Every cross-functional team at Omnea has a dedicated Product Manager and Product Designer. You'll be the connective tissue between design intent and what actually ships, and the person designers come to when they want to know what's possible.     Work with Modern Technology.  TypeScript everywhere, React and Next.js on the front end, and Meticulous for automated visual regression testing, so you can refactor the design system without fear. Behind it sits Postgres and AWS serverless infrastructure (Lambda, DynamoDB, and EventBridge), managed through Pulumi and deployed via GitHub Actions, with Datadog for observability.     AI-Native Development.  AI is core to how we build. Engineers use Claude Code and agentic workflows every day to write, review, and ship code faster, and our product is itself built on AI agents that automate complex procurement workflows.     Continuous Delivery.  We deploy small, incremental changes to production multiple times per day, enabling rapid iteration and fast customer feedback loops.     Collaboration and Autonomy.  We operate as a high-trust team where individuals are expected to take ownership while collaborating closely to solve difficult problems.     Customers at the Center.  We regularly engage directly with customers to understand their problems, gather feedback, and ensure we're building products that create genuine value.      About You      You're deep in React.  You've built complex, production React applications and you understand the framework properly, not just the API surface. Rendering behaviour, state, performance, and where things break at scale.     You've owned front-end infrastructure.  Rendering strategies, build tooling, bundle performance, and the architectural decisions underneath a large application.     You've built or owned a design system.  Not just consumed one. You've made the calls on component APIs, driven adoption across teams, and dealt with the messy reality of migration and versioning.     You have taste.  You care how things look and feel, you notice when something is only 90% right, and you can hold a genuine conversation with designers rather than just implementing tickets.     You know CSS deeply.  Layout, styling architecture, and building interfaces that hold up across breakpoints, themes, and edge cases. You treat accessibility and motion as part of the craft rather than a checklist at the end.     You're a strong engineer first.  Your depth and your interest sit in the front end, and that's the point of this role. But you're fluent in TypeScript generally and comfortable working beyond the browser when a problem calls for it.     You're motivated by impact.  You care about what your work actually achieves, not just how it's built. You thrive with the autonomy to make meaningful decisions and take real ownership of outcomes.     You're a team builder.  You're excited by maximising team performance, whether that means learning from others or taking the time to explain, give feedback, and level up those around you.     You're comfortable with ambiguity.  This role is new. Its shape will be partly yours to define, and you're happy tackling problems without a predefined solution, backed by an experienced team.      Nice-to-Haves      You've worked at design-led companies  or somewhere with a genuinely high bar for interface quality.     You've performed exceptionally  at something else, be it academics, sport, or work. You've gone above and beyond the norm.     You love engineering.  It's more than a job. You've contributed to open source or worked on side projects just because you enjoy it.      Interview Process   Before applying, we strongly encourage you to spend a few minutes in our R&D Candidate Hub. It covers our engineering culture, ways of working, interview process, tech environment, and what it's like to build at Omnea.   >> R&D Candidate Hub:   https://omnea.notion.site/R-D-Candidate-Hub-2f688cce658780f1b942c81cd3a032d4   While this is a front-end specialist role, we expect a core level understanding of  TypeScript  beyond the browser, so you should be comfortable writing general TypeScript in an exercise that will feel more full-stack than front-end. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.     Our culture:     We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.     We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.    We're a remote-first team spread across time zones, so no office to report to - work from wherever helps you do your best work. Just a couple of things to keep in mind: pay is based on where you're located, and you'll need to keep a home base in the country you're hired in. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible  within  your country, not borderless.       Location:     Remote -  United Kingdom        About the role:   As a Full Stack Engineer at Sardine, you will bridge the gap between complex technical backend systems and user-friendly interfaces to help us stop fraud in its tracks. job.description: About Doit   We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.  We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.  In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.     The Role   Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As General Manager of Doit Lithuania, you will build and run the business in Lithuania and grow it across the European Economic Area.  You will be the first senior hire in Lithuania. You will own the regulatory relationship, the build of the team, the partner network and the launch. You will sit on the management board and lead the business day to day.  We’re looking for a generalist who learns quickly, thinks deeply, and enjoys solving difficult problems in a fast-moving, regulated environment.     What You’ll Own     Own the relationship with the Bank of Lithuania and other regulators.    Build the Vilnius team, including compliance, operations and control functions.    Select and negotiate with execution, custody, fund and banking partners.    Own the business plan, financial projections, capital plan and budget.    Launch the investment platform in Lithuania and roll it out across the EEA.    Set up governance, policies and controls that meet EU and Lithuanian requirements.    Work with group leadership on product, engineering and growth.    Report to the board and take ownership of business and regulatory outcomes.       What We’re Looking For     Generalist background in consulting, investment banking, start-ups, private equity or venture capital.    Experience building or scaling a business, ideally in financial services or fintech.    Strong problem-solving skills and business judgment.    Ability to learn regulation quickly and work credibly with regulators.    Strong ownership and execution skills.    Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with boards, regulators, partners and teams.    Comfortable working across product, operations, finance and compliance.    A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a senior manager.    Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.    Curious, resourceful, and driven to build.       Nice to Have     Lithuanian language ability.    An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania.    Experience with MiFID II, brokerage, wealth management or fund distribution.    Experience building or running a regulated financial business in the EU.       This Role Is Not For     People who only want to attend meetings.    Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.    Those who need fixed scope and slow timelines.    People who avoid messy cross-functional problems.    People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.    People who see regulation as someone else’s problem.     Location   This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.  You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.     Language   English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.     Interview Process   Our process is designed to move fast:    Online assessment or practical task    Role-specific interview    CEO / final round      For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process.    Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritised.  Find more  English Speaking Jobs in France  on Arbeitnow

job.description: TLDR: We’re looking for top 1%, high agency, AI-forward graduates to join the first graduate cohort at Resonance in Berlin as AI Transformation Leads. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital, to deploy AI into the economy and rebuild businesses for the AI era. You’ll work at the frontier and solve real problems in an environment that champions ownership, autonomy and innovation at pace. Who we are Resonance is an applied AI company. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital. Our mission is to close the AI diffusion gap and rebuild businesses for the AI era. We're looking to hire Europe’s elite AI talent, and we're building our Berlin hub to serve clients across Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Why now We believe the economic diffusion of AI is the major challenge of the next decade. Foundation models are advancing far faster than organisations can absorb them; the bottleneck is embedding AI deeply into the core processes of a company to drive an inflection in pace and create organisational advantage. Europe is falling behind on AI, and we exist to help its businesses build real, defensible advantage from it rather than simply adopting it. The role As a Graduate AI Transformation Lead in Berlin, you’ll work on client teams across DACH from your first month, alongside experienced AI Transformation Leads and AI engineers, with real responsibility from day one. You’ll analyse how a business works, where time and money go, and where AI fundamentally changes the economics. You’ll build the models, business cases and story a leadership team will act on, and prototype new workflows yourself with Claude Code or similar. You’ll work side by side with engineers to define what gets built, test it with the people who will use it, and help the client’s teams adopt it. As one of our first graduate cohort, you’ll also help shape our graduate programme and how Resonance trains and grows. Your first year: Structured training in AI, consulting and the industries we work in, with coaching from Senior AI Transformation Leads and the founding team. You’ll be on a client team from your first month, in a small team where you know everyone by name and work closely with colleagues in London. Nobody expects you to know it all when you start: asking for help early is part of the job. You’ll start as a Junior Transformation Lead and typically move up a level within 18–24 months. What we’re looking for: You have extreme agency, operate with urgency, and have consistently been among the very top performers of your peers. You’re finishing an undergraduate or master’s degree in a technical subject, such as engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics or another natural science, or a quantitative subject such as economics, or you graduated in one in the last two years, with top results from a top university. You structure problems clearly and are comfortable with numbers. You use AI every day and have built something with it, whether a project, a tool or an automation, and you’re curious about how businesses actually work. You can show you make things happen through internships, a society you led, a company you started or something you built. An internship in consulting, banking, private equity or a startup is a plus, and so is German for client work in DACH. If you don’t tick every box, apply anyway. What we offer: Competitive total compensation plus equity. Real client work from your first month, learning from people who have shipped 30+ AI products and embedded AI into 50+ businesses. Every engagement ends with AI running in production and results you can measure. A team built to be one of the most talent-dense in Europe, and a chance to help close Europe’s AI gap, moving European businesses to the right side of the productivity chasm. Logistics: Berlin, 3+ days a week in the office or at client sites, mostly in DACH and Europe. English is our working language; German is a plus. We can sponsor visas for eligible candidates. Start date Summer 2027 (dates to be confirmed). We also offer Summer 2027 internships for students in the penultimate year of their degree. Apply Send your CV with your grades and a short note on something you've analysed or built with AI. We hire people from every background and judge them on what they've built. If you don't tick every box, apply anyway. Resonance is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. If you need adjustments at any stage, tell us and we'll make them.

job.description:
As an FPGA Engineer, you’ll work side-by-side with teammates to build real-world applications that power a global trading firm. You’ll create solutions with nanosecond response times, highly parallelized algorithms, and customized low-level networking that solve business challenges effectively and efficiently. Collaborating closely with our business, you’ll have in-depth insight into a problem before developing the solution.

Optiver is building with cutting edge AI technology in the most competitive, data rich landscapes in the world: financial markets. Our FPGA engineers use AI to speed up verification, debugging, and technical research, while retaining full ownership of the designs and decisions it supports.

What you’ll do

Your onboarding

You will participate in Optiver’s comprehensive Global Academy and be equipped with the knowledge needed to make an impact the moment you join your team. The comprehensive training covers trading theory and Optiver’s tech stack to hone your skills for your role. In addition, you will be paired with a dedicated mentor who will empower you to take ownership of your work and make a difference.

Your responsibilities

  • Accelerate network infrastructure and trading system components with high-speed hardware designs.

  • Research new low-latency techniques and platforms and identify opportunities for integration with our trading system.

job.description: Company   NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.  Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.  Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.  Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.   Hiring now    We are hiring as soon as possible.  This role is for someone who has already graduated, or who will complete their degree in time to start with us very soon. We are not able to consider final-year students who graduate in summer 2027 or later, and this is not a graduate scheme with a fixed annual intake.   Role Overview   This is a first full-time engineering role on the NEO-1 satellite. You will design satellite hardware and help keep the satellite's full CAD assembly organised as the design matures, learning from our lead designer and working in a small, multidisciplinary team. You will take ownership of real parts early, translate requirements into manufacturable designs and support their validation through prototyping and environmental testing.     Key Responsibilities     Design and develop mechanical hardware for the satellite, such as brackets, panels, component mounts, thermal-control hardware and cable and harness routing, with guidance from the lead designer.    Work in the satellite's large 3D CAD assembly alongside the wider design team, learning how to keep interfaces, configurations and revisions in step as several designers work in the same model.    Support assembly configuration, PLM data (3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX') or similar), bills of materials and engineering change control (ECO/ECR/ECN), so that models, drawings and interfaces stay consistent as changes are released.    Run interference and clash checks and help maintain the digital mock-up, working with each subsystem owner to allocate space and resolve conflicts.    Produce dimensioned, manufacturing-ready drawings using GD&T, with review from senior engineers.    Support design reviews (PDR and CDR) and qualification, working with structural and thermal engineers.    Work with manufacturers and suppliers to make designs easier to build, and to balance cost, mass and reliability.    Support prototype builds, integration and environmental test campaigns, iterating designs based on results.    Collaborate with electrical, software, systems and thermal engineers to integrate mechanical components into the satellite platform.     Required Skills & Experience     Bachelor's or master's degree in mechanical, aerospace or a related engineering discipline, completed or completing very soon.    Hands-on 3D CAD skills from university projects, a placement or an internship (SolidWorks preferred; CATIA, NX or Creo also considered).    Working knowledge of GD&T and experience producing engineering drawings, including from coursework or a team project.    Solid grounding in mechanical design principles, materials and thermal management, with a working understanding of structural mechanics.    Evidence of designing, building and testing something real, such as a placement project, Formula Student, a UAV, or a rocketry or satellite team, including troubleshooting and iteration.    Clear communicator who is comfortable explaining and defending design decisions, and open to feedback and challenge in a fast-moving team.     Preferred Experience     A placement, internship or year in industry in aerospace, space, motorsport or another high-reliability field.    Experience of several people working in one CAD assembly, for example in a Formula Student or university team, including how files and revisions were controlled.    Exposure to PLM or PDM systems (for example 3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX'), Windchill, Teamcenter, ENOVIA or SolidWorks PDM) or to formal engineering change processes (ECO/ECR/ECN).    Experience of design reviews, documented requirements and standards.    Satellite, CubeSat or rocketry project experience, including hardware that has launched.    Basic FEA familiarity and exposure to manufacturing processes.     Why NewOrbit Space?      Pioneering space technology  - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.     Ownership and impact  - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.     Equity and competitive salary  - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.     Comprehensive benefits  - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.     Hybrid working  - One dedicated remote day per week.     Visa sponsorship and relocation support  - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.    Find  Jobs in United Kingdom  on Arbeitnow

About Superhuman  Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. Automate GRC workflows and run compliance as code. Use Claude Code (or similar) and MCPs for evidence requests, control mapping, gap analysis, vendor reviews, and reporting; build and curate the team’s agent harness; and manage policies, control definitions, and automation in GitHub through branches, pull requests, and review.    Design control testing and drive remediation. Instrument testing across SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27017/27018, ISO 27701, PCI DSS, and ISO 42001 for continuous assurance rather than point-in-time snapshots, and work with control owners and engineering to close gaps with automated evidence behind every finding.    What Ramping Up Looks Like:  You will be configuring our GRC automation platform, not just clicking through it, within your first few weeks. In your first 90 days, we’d expect you to learn the platform configuration, ship your first automated evidence collectors, retire a batch of manual screenshot evidence, and get at least one agent-assisted workflow running end-to-end.  Why This Role:    You’ll design the automation architecture for compliance across four products, rather than maintaining an existing checklist.    You get the mandate and the tooling to retire manual evidence collection: a GRC automation platform, agentic AI, and compliance-as-code.    We actually run LLMs and AI agents in production GRC workflows today. This is how the team operates day-to-day.    Small team, high ownership, and a direct line to Legal and Engineering leadership. You’ll shape the program, not just sustain it.      Qualifications    5+ years in compliance, GRC, or IT audit, hands-on with the frameworks above (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and adjacent).    1+ year using agentic AI systems (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) to do real compliance work, with automation you have delivered, not just prototypes.    Comfortable in GitHub: repos, branches, pull requests, and code review. CI/CD familiarity is a strong plus.    Fast on new tooling. You can pick up a GRC automation platform and be productive in weeks, configuring it directly rather than relying on others to do so.    Deep GRC fluency: control design, evidence, risk, and how auditors actually think.    Working knowledge of cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP): IAM, compute, storage, networking, and security controls, because that’s where the evidence lives.    Systems thinker who prefers to automate repetitive manual work rather than repeat it.    Has a demonstrated ability to work independently with minimal guidance, proactively manages tasks and priorities across multiple projects, analyzes and executes work efficiently, collaborates effectively with cross-functional teams, and thrives in fast-paced, results-driven environments.    Nice to Have:    Reads APIs, JSON, and logs comfortably; scripting (Python, bash, TypeScript).    Prior hands-on experience with a GRC automation platform (Vanta, Drata, or similar).    Scripting/light coding and API integration experience.    Certifications such as CISA, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, or similar.    AI governance, AI risk management, or ISO 42001 exposure.    Background in a technology, SaaS, or engineering-adjacent environment.      Compensation and Benefits     Professional growth:  We believe that autonomy and trust are key to empowering our team members to do their best, most innovative work in a way that aligns with their interests, talents, and well-being. We also support professional development and advancement with training, coaching, and regular feedback.     A connected team:  Superhuman builds a product that helps people connect, and we apply this mindset to our own team. Our remote-first hybrid model enables a highly collaborative culture supported by our values. We work to foster belonging among team members in a variety of ways. This includes our employee resource groups, Superhuman Circles, which promote connection among those with shared identities including BIPOC and  LGBTQIA+  team members, women, and parents. We also celebrate our colleagues and accomplishments with global, local, and team-specific programs.     Comprehensive benefits for candidates based in Germany:  Superhuman offers all team members competitive pay along with a benefits package encompassing life care (including mental health care and risk benefits) and ample and defined time off. We also offer support to set up a home office, wellness and pet care stipends, learning and development opportunities, and more.     Relocation Support:  Superhuman provides comprehensive relocation support to make your move to Berlin seamless. As a Machine Learning Certification Researcher, you will address one of the most fundamental challenges in modern AI: proving that ML models are safe, reliable, and mathematically sound for deployment in autonomous flight. At Destinus, we are shaping the future of defense through high-speed, autonomous flight technologies. We develop next-generation unmanned aerial systems that deliver greater speed, precision, and efficiency, supporting governments and defense organizations in mission-critical operations worldwide. Daedalean AG, the AI and autonomy hub of the Destinus Group, plays a key role in this vision—developing safety-critical AI systems at the intersection of advanced research and real-world aviation. Enabling machines to perceive, understand, and make decisions in real time, we combine aerospace engineering and artificial intelligence to build the next generation of autonomous flight systems, driving innovation where it matters most.   What You'll Do   • AI Certification Strategy: Analyze our existing AI certification strategy and help adapt it—or pioneer entirely new strategies—to certify different supervised ML.  • EASA Framework Alignment: Connect mathematical guarantees, technical arguments, and model evaluations to the EASA W-shaped process for AI certification in aviation, ensuring our research aligns with the latest regulatory guidelines.  • Theoretical Foundation & Modeling: Conduct research into statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and mathematical guarantees for deep neural networks operating under dynamic real-world conditions.  • Uncertainty Quantification: Apply statistics and stochastic processes to model environmental uncertainties and sensor noise, and to quantify confidence in performance metrics.  • Literature & Proof Evaluation: Critically evaluate academic literature, mathematical proofs, and engineering assumptions with peer-review rigor to identify safety limitations and theoretical gaps in state-of-the-art AI.  • Regulatory & Audit Justification: Construct robust, logical arguments and technical justifications that translate complex, high-dimensional empirical data into structured evidence for safety audits and certification frameworks.  • Algorithmic Validation: Write clean, reproducible code in Python to test theoretical hypotheses, validate certification mechanisms, and benchmark model safety frameworks. Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. À propos du poste

En tant que leader de deuxième niveau pour l’équipe Applied AI Industries en Europe du Sud et au Moyen-Orient chez Anthropic, vous piloterez l’adoption d’une IA de frontier en partenariat avec le reste de l’organisation de mise sur le marché. Nos clients Industries en France, Ibérie et Italie incluent de nombreuses plus grandes entreprises de la région dans les services financiers, santé et sciences de la vie, fabrication, télécommunications, commerce de détail, énergie et autres secteurs. Vous mettrez à profit votre expérience de construction et de direction d’équipes de vente technique pour piloter une transformation IA positive qui répond aux besoins métier de nos clients, satisfait à leurs exigences techniques et réglementaires, et offre un haut degré de fiabilité et de sécurité.

Vous serez responsable de la direction et de la croissance de l’équipe d’architectes de solutions qui partenaire avec les directrices et directeurs de compte pour aider les entreprises à adopter et déployer les produits d’Anthropic, notamment Claude Cowork, Claude Code et la Plateforme de Développement Claude (notre API). Cela inclura l’utilisation de vos compétences techniques et votre expérience de vente consultative pour recruter d’excellentes personnes en première ligne de management et contributeurs individuels, établir des processus pour évoluer votre équipe, et représenter Anthropic directement dans les engagements clients stratégiques. Votre équipe couvre plusieurs pays et secteurs à la fois, vous serez donc responsable de la réflexion stratégique sur les comptes d’industrie complexes et de l’identification et du déploiement de solutions qui résonnent dans chaque marché, avec sa propre langue, sa culture métier et son contexte réglementaire.

Responsabilités

  • Recruter, manager et guider une équipe de managers de première ligne qui construiront à leur tour des équipes d’Applied AI Architects (H/F) de pré-vente en France, Ibérie et Italie
  • Définir les objectifs de votre équipe en collaboration avec le leadership commercial et établir les attentes de performance de base sur votre équipe
  • Agir en tant que sponsor technique et exécutif pour les clients stratégiques de haute valeur dans la région et les conseiller sur leurs stratégies globales d’adoption de l’IA ou la délimitation des cas d’usage et l’exécution de pilotes
  • Collaborer étroitement avec le leadership commercial d’Europe du Sud (couvrant également le Moyen-Orient et l’Afrique) pour construire des stratégies pour les comptes d’industrie complexes et identifier de nouvelles façons de piloter l’adoption des produits Anthropic dans des secteurs verticaux spécifiques ou des cas d’usage horizontaux
  • Aider les clients à naviguer dans les exigences réglementaires locales et européennes (par exemple, la Loi sur l’IA de l’UE, le RGPD, DORA et les attentes de résidence des données) et adapter la façon dont votre équipe s’engage à la culture métier de chaque marché
  • Travailler avec des équipes interfonctionnelles comme le produit et l’ingénierie pour assurer qu’Anthropic priorise les commentaires des clients ou résout les obstacles à l’adoption dans la région
  • Voyager régulièrement en Europe du Sud pour les clients ou conférences pour des sessions de haut niveau, des ateliers techniques et la construction de relations
  • Établir une vision commune pour créer des solutions qui permettent une IA bénéfique et sûre dans les produits technologiques
  • Contribuer à la pensée stratégique par des présentations en conférences, des webinaires et la création de contenu technique
  • Rester au courant des tendances émergentes en IA et du paysage concurrentiel

Ce profil est un bon ajustement si vous :

  • Avez 7+ ans d’expérience en gestion de pré-vente technique, incluant un leadership de deuxième niveau ou supérieur (direction de managers)
  • Avez vendu des produits techniques complexes aux grandes entreprises en France, Ibérie, Italie, Moyen-Orient et Afrique
  • Avez travaillé dans plusieurs secteurs, tels que services financiers, santé et sciences de la vie, fabrication, télécommunications, commerce de détail et énergie
  • Comprenez les différences culturelles entre les marchés d’Europe du Sud et le contexte réglementaire dans lequel opèrent vos clients, et adaptez votre approche à chacun
  • Pensez de façon hautement stratégique aux comptes d’industrie complexes et transformez cette réflexion en plans que votre équipe et vos homologues commerciaux peuvent exécuter
  • Avez une profonde maîtrise technique des cas d’usage IA en entreprise, des intégrations d’API et des déploiements LLM
  • Prospérez dans la construction et l’évolution rapide d’équipes et de processus dans des environnements ambigus et mouvants
  • Ayez d’excellentes compétences en communication, collaboration et coaching
  • Ayez une présence exécutive forte et la capacité à cultiver des relations profondes avec les leaders métier et technique des plus grandes entreprises de la région
  • Ayez au moins une familiarité de haut niveau avec l’architecture et le fonctionnement des LLM
  • Ayez une passion pour rendre les technologies puissantes sûres et bénéfiques pour la société
  • Restiez à jour et informée en vous intéressant activement à la recherche émergente et aux tendances du secteur en IA

Les candidates et candidats solides pourraient avoir :

  • Leadership de pré-vente d’entreprise à grande échelle : 5+ ans de direction d’équipes d’architectes de solutions à travers une hypercroissance (idéalement des dizaines de personnes dans plusieurs pays), avec expérience directe de direction de managers et développement de talents dans des environnements de vente de logiciels d’entreprise complexes
  • Gamme multilingue et multiculturelle : En plus de l’anglais, maîtrise d’une ou plusieurs langues parmi le français, l’italien, l’espagnol ou le portugais, et expérience de direction d’équipes distribuées dans plusieurs pays
  • Expérience avec les modèles commerciaux basés sur la consommation : Les candidats idéaux ont construit des cadres GTM ancrés sur la consommation, pas seulement sur les licences basées sur SaaS
  • Profondeur technique en IA + Engagement exécutif : Expérience pratique avec les plateformes d’IA et les modèles d’intégration d’entreprise, combinée à un historique avéré d’engagement des parties prenantes au niveau C dans des évaluations techniques de 10 M€+ et des cycles de vente d’entreprise
  • Expérience GTM multi-secteurs dans les secteurs réglementés : Succès démontré dans l’adaptation des approches techniques à différents secteurs verticaux, en particulier les secteurs réglementés tels que la banque, les assurances et la santé, y compris le travail avec les parties prenantes en matière de risque, de conformité et de comité d’entreprise

 

 

About the Role:

As the 2nd-line leader for the Applied AI Industries team in Southern Europe and the Middle-East at Anthropic, you will drive the adoption of frontier AI in partnership with the rest of the go to market organization. Our Industries customers in France, Iberia and Italy include many of the region's largest enterprises across financial services, healthcare and life sciences, manufacturing, telecom, retail, energy, and other sectors. You'll leverage your experience building and leading technical sales teams to drive positive AI transformation that addresses our customers' business needs, meets their technical and regulatory requirements, and provides a high degree of reliability and safety.

 

You will be responsible for leading and growing the solutions architect team that partners with account executives to help companies adopt and deploy Anthropic's products, including Claude Cowork, Claude Code, and the Claude Development Platform (our API). This will include leveraging your technical skills and consultative sales experience to hire great 1st line managers and individual contributors, establish processes to scale your team, and represent Anthropic directly at strategic customer engagements. Your team covers several countries and industries at once, so you will be responsible for thinking strategically about complex industry accounts and for identifying and rolling out solutions that resonate in each market, with its own language, business culture, and regulatory context.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Hire, manage, and guide a team of 1st line managers who will in turn build teams of pre-sales Applied AI Architects across France, Iberia and Italy.

  • Set goals for your team in collaboration with sales leadership and establish baseline expectations for performance across your team.

  • Act as a technical and executive sponsor for high-value strategic customers in the region and advise them on their overall AI adoption strategies or use case scoping and pilot execution.

  • Partner closely with Southern Europe sales leadership (also covering the Middle-East and Africa) to build strategies for complex industry accounts and identify new ways to drive adoption of Anthropic products within specific verticals or horizontal use cases.

  • Help customers navigate local and European regulatory requirements (for example the EU AI Act, GDPR, DORA, and data residency expectations) and adapt how your team engages to the business culture of each market.

  • Work with cross-functional teams like product and engineering to ensure Anthropic prioritizes customer feedback or resolves blockers to adoption in the region.

  • Travel regularly across Southern Europe to customers or conferences for executive-level sessions, technical workshops, and relationship building.

  • Establish a shared vision for creating solutions that enable beneficial and safe AI in technology products.

  • Contribute to thought leadership through conference presentations, webinars, and technical content creation.

  • Stay current with emerging AI trends and the competitive landscape.

 

You may be a good fit if you:

  • 7+ years of technical pre-sales management experience, including 2nd-line leadership or above (leading managers).

  • Have sold complex technical products to large enterprises in France, Iberia, Italy, the Middle-East and Africa.

  • Have worked across multiple industries, such as financial services, healthcare and life sciences, manufacturing, telecom, retail, and energy.

  • Understand the cultural differences between Southern European markets and the regulatory context your customers operate in, and adapt your approach to each.

  • Think highly strategically about complex industry accounts, and turn that thinking into plans your team and sales counterparts can execute.

  • Have deep technical proficiency with enterprise AI use cases, API integrations, and LLM deployments.

  • Thrive in building and rapidly scaling teams and processes within ambiguous and fast-moving environments.

  • Have excellent communication, collaboration, and coaching abilities.

  • Strong executive presence and ability to foster deep relationships with business and technical leaders at the region's largest companies.

  • Have at least a high level familiarity with the architecture and operation of LLMs.

  • Have a passion for making powerful technology safe and societally beneficial.

  • Stay up-to-date and informed by taking an active interest in emerging research and industry trends within AI.

 

Strong candidates may have:

  • Enterprise pre-sales leadership at scale: 5+ years leading solution architect teams through hypergrowth (ideally dozens of people across several countries), with direct experience leading managers and developing talent in complex enterprise software sales environments.

  • Multilingual and multicultural range: In addition to English, fluency in one or more of French, Italian, Spanish or Portuguese, and experience leading teams distributed across several countries.

  • Experience with consumption business models: Ideal candidates have built GTM frameworks anchored on consumption, not just SaaS-based licenses.

  • AI Technical Depth + Executive Engagement: Hands-on experience with AI platforms and enterprise integration patterns, combined with proven track record engaging C-level stakeholders in €10M+ technical evaluations and enterprise sales cycles.

  • Multi-industry GTM experience in regulated sectors: Demonstrated success adapting technical approaches to different verticals, in particular regulated ones such as banking, insurance, and healthcare, including working with risk, compliance, and works council stakeholders.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
€265.000—€310.000 EUR

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. job.description: Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.    We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.    Here’s what this particular role covers.     🛠️ About our Data Enrichment Teams   Our Data Enrichment team builds the ground-truth datasets and classifiers that describe complex driving scenes across Wayve's data corpus. Drawing on Wayve's World Foundation Model, we help teams find rare scenarios, expose performance gaps and develop better perception and driving models, supporting the safety and reliability of Wayve's ADAS and AI Driver products. As a Machine Learning Engineer, Data Enrichment, you will tackle computer vision problems spanning road geometry, spatial relationships, road users and driving behaviour.      🧠 Your day-to-day   • Work with internal customers to define scene and scenario attributes, dataset requirements and measurable acceptance criteria for annotations and classifiers  • Design and refine annotation tasks and labelling instructions, using pilots, annotator agreement and expert review to resolve ambiguity and measure quality  • Curate and deliver ground-truth datasets for other teams to train and evaluate models, addressing rare scenarios, class imbalance and coverage across countries and vehicle platforms  • Build and evaluate computer vision models that draw on Wayve's World Foundation Model to identify scene attributes and driving behaviours  • Use error analysis to identify gaps in data, labels and model performance, and test approaches to improve them      🧩 What you’ll be working on   • Ground-truth datasets and classifiers that describe road geometry, spatial relationships, road users and driving behaviour  • Integrating classifiers with enrichment infrastructure to run inference across existing and newly collected driving data, making predictions available for corpus analysis and scenario mining  • Improving reusable tools for annotation, training, evaluation and inference  • Documenting dataset and classifier quality, and communicating limitations to colleagues across disciplines      🙌 You should apply if   • You have practical experience developing and evaluating computer vision models for image or video understanding, including interpreting spatial relationships in visual data  • You have strong Python programming skills and experience with a modern machine learning framework such as PyTorch  • You have experience curating training and evaluation datasets and assessing annotation quality, with an understanding of class imbalance, data leakage and representative evaluation  • You have taken machine learning models beyond experimentation into use, with reproducible training, evaluation and inference  • You can investigate model failures and determine whether improvements need better data, clearer labels or changes to the modelling approach  • You can translate an ambiguous customer request into clear technical deliverables and quality criteria, and communicate performance and limitations to colleagues from different disciplines  • Desirable: experience with 3D geometry, multi-camera systems or temporal scene understanding; autonomous driving, ADAS or robotics; adapting pretrained, foundation or vision-language models; human annotation workflows, active learning or model-assisted labelling; SQL, distributed data processing and batch inference     🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.      More about Wayve:   🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.  Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.      How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:   Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.      🔍 The Interview Process:   Our process is clear and respectful of your time:     Initial call / recruiter screen  (30 mins)     Competency Interviews  (Programming in Python and MLE domain interview)     Deep-dive technical interviews  (systems design and hiring manager interview)     Final interview : mission & values alignment.    We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.      What’s in it for you (Location dependant):   💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually 📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve ✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable ✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs 📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth 🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more  A quick, honest note before you apply.  Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.    If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.
