job.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As Anthropic's Public Sector Sales Lead for France, you will be the face of Anthropic to the French State. This is a founding, zero-to-one role: there is no public sector team in France today, and you will build our strategy, our routes to market and our first strategic relationships from the ground up. Reporting to our EMEA South leadership, you will lead the adoption of safe, frontier AI across central government, starting with the largest ministries. You will work hand in hand with our Public Policy lead in Paris, because in few companies is policy as central to the mission as it is at Anthropic, and with Partnerships, Legal, Security and Product to put in place the commercial and compliance frameworks the State needs in order to work with us at scale.

This is a senior individual contributor role. We expect you to have run a public sector business and led teams, and to be energised by stepping back into a hands-on seat where you build it yourself and where the size of your team says nothing about the size of your scope. In the first year, success is measured less by a large number and more by putting Anthropic on the map with the French State: a clear strategy, the right foundations and our first strategic agreements.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own Anthropic's public sector go-to-market strategy for France: where we play first, how we win, and what we need to build to get there
  • Be the senior face of Anthropic to the French State, building trusted relationships with ministerial cabinets, senior officials and digital and technology leaders across the largest ministries, including defence, finance and justice
  • Own the full sales cycle on our first strategic public sector opportunities, from first engagement through procurement route, close, deployment and expansion
  • Work with Partnerships, Legal and Finance to put in place the routes to market the State needs, including resale and partner channels, framework agreements and central purchasing bodies such as UGAP
  • Partner day to day with our Public Policy lead in France so that commercial and policy engagement reinforce each other, and stay aligned with French and European AI strategy and regulation
  • Lead the conversation with customers on data sovereignty, security and compliance (for example SecNumCloud and the State's cloud doctrine), and work with Security, Legal and Product on how we meet those requirements
  • Prove value with customers alongside a shared Applied AI architect, cloud providers and systems integrators, doing much of the groundwork yourself in the early stages
  • Learn from and contribute to our UK and US public sector teams, bringing what works to France and sharing what you learn
  • Create the playbooks, references and operating rhythm that will let us scale a public sector team in France over time

You may be a good fit if you have

  • 15+ years in enterprise technology sales, including significant time running a public sector business unit or leading sales teams that sell to French central government
  • The appetite to move from a leadership role into a hands-on senior individual contributor role with no team at the outset
  • Evidence that you thrive building from zero: a new market, a new business line or an early-stage company, where systems, processes and support were not yet in place
  • A track record of landing large, complex and genuinely transformative agreements with major ministries, as the person leading the deal
  • A deep, senior network across central government, and the credibility to engage at director and cabinet level as well as with technical teams
  • Practical command of French public procurement, including tenders, framework agreements, central purchasing bodies and partner or resale routes
  • Real expertise in data sovereignty, security and compliance requirements in the French State, and experience leading those conversations with customers
  • Experience of, or a clear aptitude for, working closely with public policy or government affairs colleagues
  • Ownership and resilience: you treat what is missing as something to build, and you bring colleagues with you to build it
  • The technical curiosity to learn our products in depth and hold credible conversations with both engineering leaders and senior officials
  • Fluent French and English, with excellent written and spoken communication in both
  • Willingness to go through French security clearance (habilitation) should specific accounts require it 
  • A genuine commitment to safe and beneficial AI, and the ability to articulate why it matters for public institutions

 

À propos du poste

En tant que Responsable des ventes secteur public d'Anthropic pour la France, vous incarnerez Anthropic auprès de l'État français. Il s'agit d'un poste fondateur, à construire de zéro : il n'existe aujourd'hui aucune équipe secteur public en France, et vous bâtirez notre stratégie, nos voies d'accès au marché et nos premières relations stratégiques en partant d'une page blanche. Ce poste est rattaché à la direction EMEA Sud. Vous piloterez l'adoption d'une IA de pointe et sûre au sein de l'administration centrale, en commençant par les plus grands ministères. Vous travaillerez main dans la main avec notre responsable des affaires publiques à Paris — dans peu d'entreprises les politiques publiques sont aussi centrales à la mission que chez Anthropic — ainsi qu'avec les équipes Partenariats, Juridique, Sécurité et Produit, afin de mettre en place les cadres commerciaux et de conformité dont l'État a besoin pour travailler avec nous à grande échelle.

Il s'agit d'un poste senior de contribution individuelle. Nous attendons de vous que vous ayez dirigé une activité secteur public et encadré des équipes, et que la perspective de revenir à un poste pleinement opérationnel vous enthousiasme : un poste où vous construisez vous-même, et où la taille de votre équipe ne dit rien de l'étendue de votre périmètre. La première année, la réussite se mesurera moins à un grand chiffre qu'à votre capacité à installer Anthropic auprès de l'État français : une stratégie claire, les bonnes fondations et nos premiers accords stratégiques.

Responsabilités

  • Définir et porter la stratégie de mise sur le marché d'Anthropic pour le secteur public en France : nos premiers terrains d'action, nos leviers de succès et ce qu'il nous faut construire pour y parvenir
  • Incarner Anthropic au plus haut niveau auprès de l'État français, en nouant des relations de confiance avec les cabinets ministériels, les cadres dirigeants de l'administration et les responsables du numérique et de la technologie des plus grands ministères, dont la défense, les finances et la justice
  • Piloter l'intégralité du cycle de vente sur nos premières opportunités stratégiques dans le secteur public, du premier contact au choix de la voie de passation, jusqu'à la signature, au déploiement et à l'extension
  • Travailler avec les équipes Partenariats, Juridique et Finance pour mettre en place les voies d'accès au marché dont l'État a besoin : canaux de revente et de partenariat, accords-cadres et centrales d'achat telles que l'UGAP
  • Collaborer au quotidien avec notre responsable des affaires publiques en France, pour que les démarches commerciales et politiques se renforcent mutuellement, en cohérence avec la stratégie et la réglementation française et européenne en matière d'IA
  • Mener les échanges clients sur la souveraineté des données, la sécurité et la conformité (par exemple SecNumCloud et la doctrine « cloud au centre »), et travailler avec les équipes Sécurité, Juridique et Produit sur la façon dont nous répondons à ces exigences
  • Démontrer la valeur auprès des clients en vous appuyant sur une expertise d'architecture Applied AI mutualisée, sur les fournisseurs cloud et sur les intégrateurs, en réalisant vous-même une grande part du travail de terrain dans les premiers temps
  • Apprendre de nos équipes secteur public au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis et contribuer à leur travail, en important en France ce qui fonctionne et en partageant vos enseignements
  • Créer les playbooks, les références clients et le rythme opérationnel qui nous permettront de faire grandir une équipe secteur public en France

Ce poste peut vous correspondre si vous réunissez

  • Plus de 15 ans dans la vente de technologies aux grandes organisations, dont une période significative à la tête d'une activité secteur public ou à l'encadrement d'équipes commerciales à destination de l'administration centrale française
  • L'envie de passer d'un poste d'encadrement à un poste senior pleinement opérationnel, en contribution individuelle et sans équipe au départ
  • Un parcours qui montre que vous vous épanouissez en construisant à partir de zéro : un nouveau marché, une nouvelle ligne d'activité ou une entreprise à ses débuts, là où les systèmes, les processus et les soutiens n'existaient pas encore
  • Des accords majeurs, complexes et réellement transformateurs conclus avec de grands ministères à votre actif, en étant la personne à la tête de la négociation
  • Un réseau dense et de haut niveau au sein de l'administration centrale, et la crédibilité nécessaire pour échanger au niveau des directions et des cabinets comme avec les équipes techniques
  • Une maîtrise concrète de la commande publique française : appels d'offres, accords-cadres, centrales d'achat et voies de partenariat ou de revente
  • Une véritable expertise des exigences de souveraineté des données, de sécurité et de conformité au sein de l'État français, et l'expérience de ces échanges avec les clients
  • L'expérience — ou une aptitude manifeste — du travail en étroite collaboration avec les équipes affaires publiques ou relations institutionnelles
  • Le sens de la responsabilité et la ténacité : ce qui manque est pour vous quelque chose à construire, et vous embarquez vos collègues dans cette construction
  • La curiosité technique nécessaire pour apprendre nos produits en profondeur et tenir des échanges crédibles aussi bien avec les responsables d'ingénierie qu'avec les responsables publics de haut niveau
  • Un français et un anglais courants, avec une excellente expression écrite et orale dans les deux langues
  • La disponibilité pour engager une procédure d'habilitation de sécurité si certains comptes l'exigent
  • Un engagement sincère en faveur d'une IA sûre et bénéfique, et la capacité d'expliquer pourquoi cela compte pour les institutions publiques

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

The client is now expanding its technical architecture to build an advanced, mobile-first crypto trading platform (spot + perps) alongside a novel, original social product featuring cutting-edge mechanisms.  As the first and only engineer in this specialized domain, the incoming candidate will take an original product vision and turn it into a robust, high-performance system—holding the entire architecture and the smallest details simultaneously. The operational environment is primarily asynchronous, highly independent, and built for top-tier developers who can scale infrastructure from zero to massive daily trading volumes while maintaining absolute reliability.   Requirements     Platform Ownership:  Own the core platform, including the data layer, rewards engine, notifications, the API surface, and overall system reliability.   Trading Engine Integration:  Integrate perpetual trading engines through Hyperliquid, alongside spot trading via Jupiter and Relay.   Data Harmonization:  Aggregate and unify conflicting data providers (such as Zerion, CoinGecko, Mobula, Alchemy, and Hyperliquid) into a single, cohesive source of truth.   High-Performance Data Delivery:  Serve heavy data rapidly by implementing resilient caching mechanisms that survive traffic stampedes and fan-out structures that hold under pressure.   Cross-Chain Abstraction:  Design architecture that makes a single USDC balance across multiple chains entirely invisible and seamless to the end user.   Peak Performance & Reliability:  Maintain absolute uptime during peak market volatility; ensure the application never lags or crashes when it matters most, guaranteeing users can always close positions.   ﻿  Requirements   Proven track record of engineering resilience, including keeping a high-stakes system alive through massive traffic spikes and determining graceful degradation strategies in advance.  Extensive experience building financial rewards and accounting systems that withstand retries, prioritizing idempotency, replay safety, and precise lot tracking.  Deep understanding of end-to-end latency budgets (from a user's tap to screen rendering).  Advanced database optimization skills, capable of resolving bottlenecks directly within PostgreSQL rather than relying on secondary databases.  Strong proficiency in Rust development.  Comfortable working in a fast-paced, remote environment across North American or European timezones.    Benefits    Competitive Compensation:  Top-market base salary paired with significant equity upside.   Flexible & Remote-First Work:  100% remote working model with flexible schedules and high operational autonomy.

job.description: Take on the business and back-end operations that keep Kairos running: finances, payments, HR, compliance, and systems, plus support for our programs and Pathfinder groups.     Note:  This role description is a first draft. Scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve as our plans develop over the coming weeks, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.      About Kairos  Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:      SPAR  : The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.      Generator Residency  : In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from METR, Redwood Research, AI Futures Project, and more.      Global Challenges Project  : A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.      Pathfinder Fellowship  : Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.    We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.     The Role  We’re looking for a Generalist (Operations) to do the wide range of things that keep Kairos running in the background. The bulk of the role is core business and back-end operations: paying vendors, supervising accountants, supporting bookkeeping and our audit, figuring out how to employ and onboard people, and keeping us compliant. Alongside that, you’ll support our Pathfinder groups, process grants, build internal systems and automations, and pitch in on program ops.     What You’ll Do     Build systems and automations.  Spot the operational work that shouldn’t be done by hand and automate it, so you and the team can spend time on the things that actually need judgment.     Run our finances and back-end operations.  Pay vendors and contractors, supervise accountants, support bookkeeping and our annual audit, handle the logistics of employing people (payroll, benefits, onboarding and offboarding), and help keep us compliant. You won’t need to be an expert on day one, but you’ll learn to own these functions.     Process grants and payments.  Run grant processing across Pathfinder and our other programs, make payments to individuals and organizations, and manage expense processing.     Pitch in on program ops and whatever else needs doing.  Inbox triage, problem-solving on program logistics, and the occasional program-ops crunch where we need the hands.       Who You Are     Smart, agentic, and able to figure things out.  A lot of this role is picking up unfamiliar processes (a new accounting task, a compliance requirement, a group’s odd request) and just working out how to do them well. We care about this more than about specific prior experience.     Great at automation and tooling.  You instinctively reach for a better system rather than resigning yourself to doing things by hand, and you use AI and automation tools to get more done, complementing rather than replacing your own judgment. The best person in this role makes much of the repetitive work disappear.     Eager to help, and able to be assertive.  You like unblocking people and improving their experience. You can be gentle but honest with a rejected applicant, and politely firm with an overly demanding one.     Organized and on top of things.  You keep careful track of to-dos and information. When you drop a ball, it’s on purpose.     Strong writer and communicator.  You’re clear and concise, and you think through your messaging from the reader’s perspective.     Mission-aligned.  You care about making advanced AI go well, and you’re comfortable operating in the AI safety ecosystem and its culture.    While not required, we especially value:    Some experience in finance, accounting, HR, nonprofit compliance, event planning, or other business operations or nonprofit administration (but we’re glad to have you learn these on the job)    Strong automation and AI-tooling chops    Context on AI safety and the broader ecosystem       Why Work With Us    You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The programs you’ll support influence hundreds of future AI safety and policy professionals.    Few ops roles are this broad. You’ll touch grants, finance, compliance, systems, and programs, and build unusually wide operating experience fast.    You’ll get to shape the role around your interests, with a say in which skills you build and which functions you take on.    We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.    Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers.       What We Offer     Base salary : $95,000–$190,000, depending on experience and location, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates     Location : Access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston; optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses.     Benefits : Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget     Team retreats:  We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.       Logistics     Start date : Flexible, though we generally expect new hires to be able to start within a couple of months of applying    Remote, with expected travel 3-6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US    We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, though we have a light preference for people to work out of Berkeley.    We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).    We may be able to provide visa sponsorship to the US, depending on the circumstances (especially, but not exclusively, O-1As).       Our Culture  We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.  We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.     Application Process    Application form (10–20 mins)    Screening call (15 mins)    Take-home assignment (1.5–3 hours, paid)    Interview (45 mins)    Reference checks    Work trial (3–4 days, paid - this can be flexibly scheduled around your other commitments)    Offer    If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.     Questions? Reach out at   Know someone who might be a good fit?  If your referral gets hired and completes 6 months with us, we’ll pay you a $5,000 referral bonus.  Learn more here .   Compensation: $95K – $190K    • $95K – $190K   Find  Jobs in Germany  on Arbeitnow

job.description: About Hilo by Aktiia High blood pressure is the world's most common disease, causing 18M deaths each year. At Hilo by Aktiia, we're building a world where no lives are lost to its effects — with technology that helps people take control of their health. We're a venture-backed scale-up with $96M raised from investors in Europe and the US. Rooted in 18 years of research at the Swiss Center for Electronics and Microtechnology (CSEM), our device is the world's only medically accurate, cuffless, continuous blood pressure monitor for daily use — clinically validated and CE Marked as a Class IIa medical device, now available in 12 countries. In July, we launched in the US. We're a remote-first company headquartered in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, united by our passion for impact and innovation. Applicants must already hold a valid visa or work permit for their country of residence, as Hilo is not able to provide visa sponsorship. About the role Hilo is looking for an experienced Human Factors Project Manager to own all of our human factors and usability work. Right now that work is split across Product, Design, Clinical Operations, QARA and outside agencies, and no single person is accountable for it. You'll be that person. You'll coordinate the specialists, keep work moving between teams and make sure every deliverable meets the quality and regulatory standard. That frees our domain teams to get back to their own work. What you'll own Usability studies: You'll own the study calendar, protocols and relationships with external labs such as Sage Research. This covers formative and summative studies across hardware and software, including FDA submission work for Hilo Medical. You'll make sure findings get back to design on a regular schedule. IFU and Quick Start Guide: You'll decide what content goes in the QSG, the app and the IFU. You'll also own version control and localisation (Phrase, Novalins) and brief and manage freelance designers and print partners. Packaging: You'll own packaging briefs from start to finish and coordinate agencies (ARD, Superhuit, Carac Design) and freelance packaging designers. You'll keep the work aligned with regulatory, cost and manufacturing constraints. Clinical studies: You'll connect the human factors evidence from ClinOps-run trials with the human factors evidence for the product we ship to customers. Roadmap and reporting: You'll keep a single human factors roadmap and manage dependencies, resourcing and budgets across teams. Each month you'll report confidence levels and raise any risks to leadership. This is a part time contractor role of up to three days per week, with a total fee of CHF 17,500 for the initial engagement. We would like to start as soon as possible, with a review after three months. Requirements What you'll bring Human factors or usability engineering experience in medical devices, ideally with wearables or connected health Proven project or programme management: you've owned the plan, sequenced multiple workstreams and delivered on deadlines through others Hands-on knowledge of IEC 62366 usability engineering, use-related risk documentation (e.g. UFMEAs) and IFU development Experience managing agencies, labs and freelancers Clear, confident communication, with a track record of connecting Product, Clinical and Quality/Regulatory teams First priorities Audit of our current processes and human factors function Set up the usability study calendar Get a decision on the content split for the QSG "5-minute sheet" redesign Nice to have: FDA submission experience, a UX research background, and familiarity with InDesign/Figma localisation workflows Benefits At Hilo by Aktiia, our values guide everything we do: Move the Needle — You focus on what drives real impact. You let data and clarity guide your decisions, and you take accountability for results. You're a difference maker — you drive ideas to commercial success from start to end. Move Fast, Learn, Refine — You work with urgency and purpose, balancing speed with quality. You treat feedback as a chance to learn, and you're deep in customer and partner feedback — translating it to action quickly. Team First — You collaborate effectively across teams and build trust through clarity and respect. You're comfortable bridging local execution with a global team, and you communicate openly across time zones.

you actively own processes end to end and think deeply about how they interact with other parts of the product and the people around you    Comfortable working with (or learning to work with) AI-assisted tooling such as Claude, Github Co-Pilot or Cursor    Strong observability and performance mindset and experience being able to quantify and show how your products are used    Familiarity with CI/CD and common DevOps processes    Collaborative and curious - Applicants must already hold a valid visa or work permit for their country of residence, as Hilo is not able to provide visa sponsorship.     Role Overview    As Influencer Marketing Manager, you will develop and run Hilo’s influencer marketing program across our key markets. You will find creators whose voices and audiences fit our brand, negotiate effective partnerships, and shape content that makes Hilo relevant and credible. The role combines brand and performance: you will use data to estimate the potential of each partnership before we invest, measure its results, and apply what you learn to future campaigns.  Work location: Our company operates on a remote-first model. This role can be performed remotely from anywhere in Europe. Fluent English and German are a must. Occasional travel to our office in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, or to team events may be required.   Core Responsibilities    Identify, assess, and recruit creators across relevant platforms and markets.  Develop campaign concepts that balance Hilo’s brand goals with measurable commercial outcomes.  Forecast likely reach, engagement, traffic, and acquisition outcomes to guide creator selection and budgets.  Negotiate fees, deliverables, timelines, and content usage rights, including rights to use creator content in paid campaigns.  Manage partnerships end to end, from briefing and content review through publication and reporting.  Build and nurture long-term relationships with creators and brand ambassadors to drive sustained awareness, trust, and advocacy.  Collaborate with paid media teams to amplify high-performing creator content across paid social and other relevant channels.  Set clear goals, track brand and performance metrics, and compare results with initial estimates.  Use campaign data and audience insights to improve creator selection, content formats, and investment decisions.  Work across marketing and product to align campaigns with Hilo’s priorities and approved health claims.  Build repeatable processes that support growth across the US, UK, Germany, and other markets.    Requirements     Background & Experience     At least 2 years of hands-on influencer or creator marketing experience, including managing partnerships from start to finish.  A data-driven mindset: you can estimate campaign outcomes, assess performance, and turn findings into better decisions.  Strong creative judgment and an understanding of how creator content builds both brand trust and customer demand.  Strong negotiation skills and confidence working with creators and their representatives.  Excellent communication, organization, and attention to detail.  Fluency in English; German is a plus.  Experience in health tech, wellness, medical devices, or another category where trust and accurate claims matter is welcome.    Benefits     What Makes You A Great Fit    At Hilo by Aktiia, our values guide everything we do:    Move the Needle  — You focus on what truly drives impact for our customers and company. You use data and clarity to guide your decisions and prioritize what matters most. You push boundaries with bold, thoughtful innovation and hold yourself accountable for results.   Move Fast, Learn, Refine  — You work with urgency and purpose, balancing speed with high quality. You treat mistakes as learning opportunities, experiment thoughtfully and iterate quickly. You take ownership, act hands-on and always look for smarter, faster ways to get things done, including leveraging AI and new tools.   Team First  — You put the team above individual interests, building trust through openness and respect. You encourage healthy debate, challenge directly while caring personally and stand behind team decisions. You act as an owner, stepping in when needed and doing what’s necessary for the team’s success.    Why Join Us?     Hilo by Aktiia is becoming one of the most important med-tech companies and you can be part of this exciting story.  Work on a mission that matters: transforming cardiovascular health at global scale.  Be part of a high-impact, fast-growing, and venture-backed scale-up company.  Collaborate with a diverse, passionate and talented team.  Competitive compensation, equity program and other benefits (depending on location).    Ready to Move the Needle?   If you are passionate about making a meaningful impact in people's lives and excel in an environment where individuals take ownership and are committed to delivering results, we are happy to receive your application. job.description: Join Neudata - Research Analyst      Introducing Neudata:   Neudata is the global leader in alternative and market data intelligence, helping investors, hedge funds and corporates discover, evaluate, and use data to make smarter decisions. Our independence is what really sets us apart - we provide objective, unbiased intelligence that our clients trust and depend on.  Neudata’s research team is at the core of what we do. Clients of Neudata have access to:    Our research portal, allowing them to browse our catalogue of dataset reports, each of which is written by a member of the research team and pertaining to a dataset (e.g. short positions data by vendor X)    Our research team’s expertise, allowing us to help them make informed data decisions (e.g. through calls where we share our opinion on the most appropriate dataset for their needs)       The Role:   Our expertise lies in the vast world of alternative data, spanning everything from social sentiment feeds and credit card transactions to complex ESG signals. As a Research Analyst, you will join the team dedicated to  Scout , our premier platform for alternative data discovery. Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with a fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house, hardware and software. job.description:
Build the next generation of autonomous construction robotics  
 At MESH, we develop autonomous robotic systems that automate end-to-end rebar construction. Bridging digital design and physical automation, our multidisciplinary team transforms advanced robotics research into robust, production-ready industrial systems deployed globally. 
 Tasks 
  Role description  
 We are looking for a Robotics Software Engineer to develop and productize software across the full robotics stack from perception and motion planning to control and system integration. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who enjoys working across subsystem boundaries. You will take ownership of the engineering work required to turn promising research and algorithms into robust and mature capabilities that can be deployed and maintained in real-world robotic systems. 
 What You Will Work On 
 You will contribute across the full robotics software stack, including: 
 
 Perception: 2D/3D sensing, point-cloud processing, object and feature detection, pose estimation, calibration. 
 Motion Planning: collision checking, trajectory generation and optimization, kinematics, robot/world modeling, and integration of planning algorithms. 
 Robot Control: integration with industrial robot controllers, HAL layers, trajectory execution, real-time or near-real-time control interfaces, state monitoring, and coordination of multi-robotic systems. 
 System Integration: connecting robotics SW, application logic, hardware, and external systems into reliable end-to-end robotic applications. 
 Robotics Infrastructure: reusable software components, interfaces, configuration, logging, diagnostics, testing, simulation, and deployment infrastructure. 
 
 Your Responsibilities 
 
 Design, implement, test, and maintain robotics software primarily in C++ and Python. 
 Develop and integrate components across the full robotics SW stack. 
 Take algorithms and prototypes and mature them into reliable software components. 
 Build automated tests, simulation-based tests, hardware-in-the-loop tests, and system-level validation where appropriate. 
 Work with industrial robots, sensors, cameras, external axes, and other automation hardware. 
 Develop clean interfaces between robotics algorithms, hardware drivers, application software, and higher-level systems. 
 Diagnose complex problems that span software, algorithms, networking, robot controllers, sensors, and hardware. 
 Improve observability through structured logging, diagnostics, error reporting, and system health monitoring. 
 Support deployment, commissioning, troubleshooting, and validation of robotic systems. 
 
 Requirements 
  What We Are Looking For  
 Required 
 
 Masters degree or higher in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or a related field. 
 Strong software engineering skills in C++, with working knowledge of Python. 
 Experience developing software for robotic or other complex hardware systems. 
 Good understanding of several areas of robotics, such as, motion and trajectory planning, robot control, vision, sensor and robot calibration. 
 Experience with robotics middleware such as ROS/ROS2 or similar 
 Comfortable working with Linux and modern software development workflows using Git, code reviews, build systems, debugging tools, and automated testing. 
 Ability to debug problems across multiple layers of a robotic system rather than treating individual components in isolation. 
 Strong understanding of software architecture, modularity, interfaces, and maintainability. 
 
 Experience in one or more of the following would be an advantage: 
 
 3D perception using point clouds, depth cameras, stereo systems. 
 Libraries such as Eigen, PCL, OpenCV, or similar. 
 Collision detection, robot/world modeling, trajectory optimization, or numerical optimization. 
 Real-time or high-performance robot communication and control. 
 Profiling, performance optimization, concurrency, and multithreaded C++. 
 Deploying and supporting robotic systems outside a controlled R&D environment. 
 CI/CD and automated testing for robotics software. 
 Experience working with industrial robotic arms such as ABB 
 
 We do not expect you to be an expert in every part of the robotics stack. We are looking for strong software engineering fundamentals, depth in one or more robotics areas, and the ability and interest to work across subsystem boundaries. 
  Eligibility  
 Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Switzerland or be eligible to obtain the required Swiss work authorization without employer-sponsored visa support. 
  Why Join MESH?  
 At MESH, you will work on robotics problems where advanced R&D meets real-world industrial deployment. Our goal is not only to develop new robotics capabilities, but to turn them into systems that solve challenging problems in real world deployments. 
 
 You will have opportunities to work across the full robotics SW stack including system integration, and the software architecture connecting them rather than being restricted to a narrow subsystem. 
 You will work directly on the engineering challenges that take robotics from promising prototypes to robust, repeatable, and deployable solutions. 
 Solve challenging real-world robotics problems. Work with industrial robots, 3D vision systems, complex environments, and applications where conventional automation approaches reach their limits. 
 See your work operate on real hardware. Develop software that moves beyond simulation and demos and becomes part of robotic systems deployed in real production environments. 
 Have impact across the system. As part of a small, multidisciplinary engineering team, you will work closely across robotics, software, and hardware, with the opportunity to influence both technical decisions and how our robotics platform evolves.

job.description: Company   NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.  Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.  Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.  Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.   Role Overview   You will design satellite structure and hardware, and help keep the satellite's full CAD assembly organised and under control as the design matures. Working within a small, multidisciplinary team, you will translate requirements into manufacturable designs and support their validation through prototyping and environmental testing.      Key Responsibilities     Design and develop mechanical hardware for the satellite, including secondary structures (panels, brackets and component mounts), thermal-control hardware, cable and harness routing, and mechanisms. Primary structure experience is welcome.    Work in the satellite's large 3D CAD assembly alongside the wider design team, using top-down design and skeleton models to keep interfaces, configurations and revisions in step as several designers work in the same model.    Manage assembly configuration, PLM data (3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX') or similar), bills of materials and engineering change control (ECO/ECR/ECN), so that models, drawings and interfaces stay consistent as changes are released.    Run interference and clash checks and maintain the digital mock-up, working with each subsystem owner to allocate space and resolve conflicts.    Produce fully dimensioned, manufacturing-ready drawings and interface control documents using GD&T.    Support design reviews (PDR and CDR) and qualification, working with structural and thermal engineers on analysis and verification planning.    Optimise designs for manufacturability, cost, mass and reliability, working directly with manufacturers and suppliers.    Support prototype builds, integration and environmental test campaigns, iterating designs based on results.    Collaborate with electrical, software, systems and thermal engineers to integrate mechanical components into the satellite platform.        Required Skills & Experience     Bachelor's degree in mechanical, aerospace or a related engineering discipline.    3+ years' experience in mechanical design of aerospace, space or other high-reliability hardware, with strong 3D CAD skills (SolidWorks preferred; CATIA, NX or Creo also considered).    Practical application of GD&T and experience producing manufacturing-ready drawings.    Solid grounding in mechanical design principles, materials and thermal management, with a working understanding of structural mechanics.    Demonstrated ability to design, build and test hardware, including troubleshooting and iteration.    Clear communicator who is comfortable explaining and defending design decisions, and open to feedback and challenge in a fast-moving team.       Preferred Experience     Satellite or spacecraft design, ideally detailed design of secondary structures (panel and component mounting, thermal hardware, cable and harness routing). Primary structure experience is a plus.    Experience working in large, multi-person CAD assemblies, including top-down design, skeleton or master models, in-context references and configurations.    Experience with PLM or PDM systems (for example 3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX'), Windchill, Teamcenter, ENOVIA or SolidWorks PDM), configuration management, revision control and formal change processes (ECO/ECR/ECN).    Experience working within formal engineering processes, such as design reviews, documented requirements and standards.    Hardware that has launched.    Basic FEA familiarity, MGSE or ground-support equipment design, and electromechanical packaging.     Why NewOrbit Space?      Pioneering space technology  - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.     Ownership and impact  - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.     Equity and competitive salary  - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success. job.description: Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.    The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But international fintechs and banks are left with two unsatisfying options to choose from: Either build on legacy correspondent banks that are slow and unreliable, or interface with middleware providers that neither move nor hold the dollars directly, but instead rely on underlying legacy banks themselves. At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.   We are a group of ex-founders, founding employees of unicorns, and people who dropped out of university because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and Etched.   We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.     The Role   You will own security engineering end-to-end across application, infrastructure, and incident response: partnering with product and platform teams during design, writing and shipping security automation in production, and leading high-quality response when something breaks. Day to day, you will help define security in a greenfield modern bank, moving beyond threat modeling, harden cloud and CI/CD paths, build detection and response workflows, and drive remediation to closure with clear risk tradeoffs. This role reports to the CISO. What matters most is measurable risk reduction that keeps product velocity high.      Your First Six Months   Understand the foundations and increase your ownership rapidly.     Months 1-2:   Enforce an SSDLC that codifies existing security goals across EU-live payment/ledger services and US launch-critical services into required design, build, and release checkpoints (ownership, control evidence, and exception handling), with 100% of net-new Tier-1 changes following the workflow.     Months 3-4:  Stand up an AI-native product-security review pipeline that auto-triages code/dependency/IaC findings by service criticality, proposes fixes in pull requests, and routes owner-tagged remediation tasks  and reduces non-actionable security alerts.     Months 5-6:  Expand baseline coverage to >=85% of Tier-1 services for workload identity hardening, secret management standards, runtime audit logging, and high-severity dependency monitoring; start monthly control-evidence reporting to Security & Compliance.       Who Will Thrive At Augustus   We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:     American Dream:  You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.     Live Player:  You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.     Ever to Excel:  You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.     Genuine:  You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.        This role is for you if:     You can point to security automation you personally built that replaced recurring manual review work.    You have strong product security fundamentals and can improve secure-by-default patterns in fast-moving engineering teams.    You have led end-to-end rollout of security controls in production, from design and implementation through adoption and evidence.    You regularly influence architecture decisions before launch through fast, lightweight risk reviews and pragmatic controls.    You are comfortable writing production-grade code or infrastructure changes, not only policy or tickets.    You use AI tooling to accelerate security reviews and remediation planning without lowering quality or signal.    You push ambiguous work forward without waiting for a complete playbook, and you bring stakeholders with you. An interest in the people who use the product : you ask who it’s for and how you’ll know it worked.     Clear writing : a PR description or a short note that a teammate (or an agent) could act on without asking you. Own the outcome : Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.     Go further together : Collaboration, respect and different perspectives. About the role   For 10 weeks, you’ll work alongside our engineers on real software, shipping features that real customers use. You’ll be part of the day-to-day life of the team, with the support and room to learn what a first role in software deserves.  • Pair with engineers, get your code reviewed (and review theirs), and take part in standups, planning and retros.  • Work on the same things as everyone else, using the same tools, including AI tools like Claude.  • Spend every Friday afternoon (10% of your time) on learning, whether that’s lightning talks, a community of practice or building something of your own.  • Last year’s interns merged code in their first week, shipped a feature customers had been asking for, fixed a customer support issue, ran team standups and retros, gave a talk to the wider company, and learned C# and .NET on the job to build their own project.   “I didn’t feel like an intern, I really felt like part of the team.”   Kris Sananpanichkul, past software intern      What makes you a great fit   You don’t need to tick every box. It’s fine if you don’t.  •  Something you’re proud of:  something you’ve built, fixed or figured out. It could be a uni project, a side project, a game mod, a Discord bot or a tricky bug. job.description: Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.    We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.    Here’s what this particular role covers.      🛠️ About our Map & Route Team   Our Map & Route team sits within Wayve’s Automotive Platforms division in Vehicle Software Engineering, and builds the geospatial foundations behind our AI driver. Working with global-scale data, the team turns road-network and navigation data into reliable products used across Wayve, building geospatial services and data products to support company operations. We work with our model development, experimentation, and evaluation platforms to build an AI driver that uses maps and navigation data like an expert human driver by using map information to enhance training and evaluation of performance. We are a full-stack team owning mapping end to end, getting to touch work that is infrastructure, data engineering, data science, backend and frontend.      🧠 Your day-to-day     Write full-stack services in Python and Typescript, creating novel geospatial services to solve challenging and unique problems we face in building our AI driving products.    Collaborate with internal teams to understand requirements and build solutions with global geospatial data.    Design and build data pipelines with PySpark and Databricks to enrich fleet data with mapping and road-network information at global scale.    Build applications and datasets that support route planning and the preparation of map data for training and simulation.    Integrate with navigation and mapping APIs from providers such as Mapbox, TomTom and Google Maps.    Maintain, support and improve the services the team already runs.    Deploy and operate your services on Azure and Kubernetes, owning them end to end.        🧩 What you’ll be working on     Global-scale geospatial enrichment pipelines that tell us where we’ve driven and what the road network looks like.    Route-planning applications and datasets that help our teams decide where to drive next.    Map data preparation for model training and simulation.    New services you’ll take from idea to production and lead end to end.        🙌 You should apply if     You are a strong, hands-on Python engineer who can deliver high-quality production code at pace.    You are comfortable with an AI-assisted or AI engineering workflow (ideation, planning, implementation and review).    You have built and operated large-scale data pipelines using Spark or PySpark.    You are comfortable writing SQL to query and analyse large datasets.    You have working knowledge of cloud infrastructure and container orchestration, ideally Azure and Kubernetes, and are happy to own deployment, monitoring, and observability of your services.    You enjoy taking ownership of new services and seeing them through end to end.    Experience with geospatial data processing, road-network data or routing engines (e.g. OpenStreetMap, TomTom, HERE or Overture data, PostGIS, navigation APIs) would be a strong advantage.    Experience with Bazel or monorepo build systems is desirable but not mandatory.    Experience with workflow orchestration tools such as Flyte or Airflow would be a bonus.       🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.      More about Wayve:   🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.  Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. job.description:
The Opportunity  
  The infrastructure that runs the modern world (power grids, data centres, fibre networks, EV charging) is being built out faster than at any point in a generation. The companies doing that work are drowning in the volume, variety, and velocity of it. Sitetracker is how they stay ahead of it.  
   
  Sitetracker is the AI-native platform for infrastructure lifecycle management, covering project, construction, operations, and asset management in one system of record. Scout, our enterprise AI agent platform, is what sets us apart. Scout does the work, not just reports on it, and it stays grounded in the customer's own data so the answers are trustworthy enough to act on. That is what holds up in an enterprise procurement review when a bolted-on chatbot does not.  
   
  You will be our go-to Strategic Account Executive for the Middle East territory. Your job is to grow revenue and to shape how Sitetracker leads the AI-native transformation of digital infrastructure across the Middle East. You will own a priority territory with strong product-market fit, backed by proven customer outcomes, a differentiated platform, and strong demand generation.  
   
  Our top performers work as enterprise advisors. They bring strategic thinking, curiosity, and real customer empathy. They own outcomes, not quotas. If you raise the bar, love winning new logos, and want autonomy, scale, and purpose, this is a role worth a serious look.  
   
  What You'll Do  
  You will join a sales team that pairs start-up pace with enterprise ambition. This is a build role, not an inherited book of business. You will define and execute the go-to-market strategy for your territory, engage new prospects, and guide them through high-stakes decisions with precision and insight.  
   
  Every deal moves the industry forward, whether that is energising a new grid interconnection, standing up a data centre, upgrading a telecom network, or scaling EV charging. You will orchestrate complex buying journeys across large stakeholder groups, partner cross-functionally with product, marketing, and services, and earn the trust of executives on both sides. This is a quota-carrying role in a MEDDPICC environment, and it is also a chance to lead, to sell a genuinely differentiated platform, and to leave a mark.  
   
  You will be selling into a market that is actively rethinking how it uses AI. Part of the job is separating signal from hype: showing skeptical enterprise buyers what agentic AI grounded in their own operational data actually changes about how their teams work, and what it is worth.  
   
  The Skills You'll Have

  Demonstrates evidence of selling in the Middle Eastern markets

job.description: Deducta    Strategy & Operations    Location:  London, UK, near London Bridge. Hybrid, 3-4 in-person days a week.   Compensation:  £90k-£110k base salary plus equity   Visa Sponsorship:  Available for the right candidate   Start Date:  As soon as possible   Why we exist   Every decision a business makes, from the suppliers it trusts to the risks it accepts, eventually shows up as spend. This makes spend data the most honest record of how a company operates. Not the strategy deck or the org chart: spend describes what really happened.  This record exists, but it's scattered across dozens of systems and decades of legacy technology. Companies spending billions a year still can't easily answer: Who are our suppliers? Where are we exposed? What are we paying for twice?  We believe a business that can't see itself clearly can't make great decisions. Deducta exists to give the world's most complex organisations a true picture of how they operate, and the intelligence to act on it. Our ambition is to become the category-defining platform for enterprise data intelligence.  We're well funded, growing fast, and have already processed more than £1 trillion of spend for some of the world's largest and most recognisable companies. Our partners use Deducta to deliver major business transformations orders of magnitude faster.   Why this role matters   Deducta is growing fast, and the work that keeps a company running well at this pace rarely belongs to one function. This role works directly with the Chief of Staff on the company's top priorities, turning them into plans, decisions and results. You'll report to the Chief of Staff.  You'll have broad scope and real autonomy, moving between operating cadences, cross-functional projects, investor materials and analysis for the leadership team. You'll see how every part of the company works and help shape how it runs.   What you'll do      Company priorities:  Turn the leadership team's priorities into clear plans with owners, milestones and measures, and keep them on track.     Operating cadences:  Run and improve how we plan, set goals and review progress, from weekly leadership meetings to quarterly planning.     Cross-functional projects:  Lead projects that span GTM, customer delivery and hiring, from scoping the problem through to results.     Board and investor materials:  Prepare board decks, investor updates and the analysis behind them.     Analysis for leadership:  Build the models, benchmarks and recommendations the leadership team uses to make decisions.     Success in this role means:      Priorities deliver:  Company priorities have clear owners and plans, and progress is visible without chasing.     Cadences work:  Planning and review cycles run on time and lead to decisions rather than status updates.     Projects land:  Cross-functional projects finish with measurable results, and the processes they create keep working.     Trusted analysis:  Leadership relies on your analysis and recommendations for its most important decisions.     Who you are   We're looking for a high-agency former management consultant with roughly three to four years in MBB or top-tier management consulting, ideally having reached Manager. You'll combine structured problem solving with the drive to execute. A background in procurement or enterprise software isn't required.   You might be the right fit if you have:      Top-tier consulting experience:  Roughly three to four years at MBB or a top-tier strategy firm, with experience leading workstreams and working with senior clients.     Structured problem solving:  You take an ambiguous problem, break it down and turn it into a clear plan with owners and milestones.     Analytical depth:  You build models and analysis yourself, and turn them into clear recommendations.     Strong execution:  You follow through on details, keep many workstreams moving at once, and build processes that run without you.     Executive communication:  You write and present clearly to senior audiences, including boards and investors.     Range:  You're comfortable moving between strategy and hands-on operations in the same week.     Nice to have:  Startup or in-house strategy experience, or exposure to B2B software, data or AI.    We care most about how you think, the quality of your work and how you approach unfamiliar problems. Previous startup experience isn't essential, but the pace, initiative and judgement to thrive in one are.   How we work   We believe in freedom and responsibility. We set clear priorities, share the context and trust people to decide how to deliver. You'll thrive here if you value:     Ownership:  You own the outcome, not just the task. You deliver what you commit to, follow through when things get difficult, and own your mistakes.     Unreasonable hospitality:  You treat prospects, clients and teammates with exceptional care as a default. You anticipate needs, communicate with clarity, and help others succeed.     Bias for action:  We don’t have every answer upfront. You move things forward without waiting to be asked, take calculated risks, and adapt as you learn.     Craft:  Moving quickly matters, but so does doing work that stays clear, reliable and useful as we grow.     System building:  You create leverage beyond your own output, building processes, tools and documentation that others reuse and that keep working without you.     Candor:  You tell the hard truth early, give and receive feedback thoughtfully, ask for help when you need it, and push back when priorities need to change.     Curiosity about AI:  You’re excited by what applied AI makes possible, and you look for ways to use it in your own work.    As an early team member, you'll help shape our culture, our processes and where Deducta goes next. We're growing quickly, and this role will grow with us. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.      About Kaluza   Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.    Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.    With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.     The role   You’ll join the Kaluza Technology community: a large team of product-focused and data-led Product and Platform Engineers working at serious scale. Our ecosystem is primarily based on TypeScript and React, utilising GraphQL and Kafka, backed by AWS and Terraform. Our work and responsibilities are diverse and wide-ranging, so you will need to have a product-minded problem solving attitude first and foremost .  As a Senior Engineer you’ll own a slice of the product end-to-end, from the first design conversation to running it in production, and you’ll build it with AI coding agents as your default. We’re looking for someone whose judgement is worth more than their typing speed.    Engineers at Kaluza build with AI, and we mean that practically. From your first day you’ll have paid access to Claude Code, with a budget we don’t ration, and MCP access to the systems you need. Our tooling and conventions are evolving quickly, and you’ll have a heavy hand in defining how we build moving forward.     What you’ll do      Set the technical direction for your team : be accountable for the solution designs and architecture decisions, work with your team on technical strategy, and assist them through ambiguity over the longer term.     Work across the stack over time:  depending on the team you’ll work across the interface people use, the services behind it, and the APIs between them, in whatever stack your team runs.     Build with AI coding agents as your default:  break work down so agents can execute it, direct them, review what they produce as carefully as a colleague’s PR, and maintain the tests and guardrails that let agent-written code merge safely.     Own the health of your services : SLOs and SLAs, operational health reviews, post-mortems, and the in-hours support rota, with your turn on the on-call rota alongside the team.     Coach the engineers around you : technical guidance for a mix of junior and senior engineers, pairing, and code review that teaches as well as gates.     Connect your team to the rest of Kaluza : work with other Tech Leads and Principal Engineers on the wider architecture, and represent your team where platform decisions and engineering standards are made.       What you’ll bring   These are the practices and behaviours we see most in our best tech leads and value deeply, but we don’t expect everyone to tick every single box. If you’re excited by the role and can see yourself thriving here, we’d love to hear from you.    Ideally, you’ll have:     Experience with our tech stack:  TypeScript and React, utilising GraphQL and Kafka, backed by AWS and Terraform.     Experience leading technical change : you’ve taken a new service or a major architecture change from idea through to running in production, and you can say what you’d do differently.     A daily agentic development practice : you build with tools like Claude Code or Cursor, you can walk us through work you’ve shipped this way, and you have views on where agents help a team and where they get in the way.     Operational ownership : comfortable deploying with shared tooling, well-versed in SRE fundamentals like SLOs, disaster recovery and platform health monitoring, and used to owning your software in production, including out-of-hours on-call.     A coach’s instincts : you’ve mentored and grown engineers at different levels, and you make the people around you better.     Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to action : you can deliver against a technical strategy iteratively over months, and you’d rather ship a sound first step than wait for certainty.     Strong product sense : you ask why before building, and you can point to times when user feedback or metrics changed what you shipped.     Clear communication, especially in writing : designs, specs, PR descriptions and post-mortems that a teammate, a stakeholder or an agent can act on, and the stakeholder skills to work well with Product Managers, Principal Engineers and other Tech Leads.       Our Values   Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:     Play to win : Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.     Solve the real problem : Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.     Build trust every day : Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.     Own the outcome : Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.     Go further together : Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.       Our Perks     Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period    Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests    Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work    Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget    Climate: Furthr, our climate action app       Come as you are   We want to meet people from all walks of life. job.description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.  As a Fluidic Components Technical Owner, you will own the technical follow-up of suppliers providing assigned Nyx Earth fluid-control equipment, including the technical baseline, evidence path, supplier development and qualification path, delivery readiness, integration support, and operations feedback loop.  You will work closely with propulsion system engineering, equipment owners, program management, procurement, quality, PA, supplier quality, AIT/MAIT, test, M&P, safety, operations, and suppliers or manufacturing partners providing the assigned components. The reporting line is to be confirmed by Propulsion leadership.    Key Responsibilities    Own the assigned fluidic-component technical baseline, including requirements, interfaces, verification methods, qualification logic, review data, and acceptance criteria.    Maintain a system-level view of fluidic, mechanical, thermal, electrical, command, cleanliness, materials-compatibility, safety, operations, and integration interfaces.    Follow supplier development, qualification, acceptance, integration, and operations-support logic for assigned valves, regulators, fill/drain equipment, pressure-control equipment, or related fluidic components.    Keep TEC's technical position clear when following suppliers, manufacturing partners, special processes, or test houses.    Review supplier deliverables, drawings where available, analyses, procedures, inspection evidence, test results, review packages, deviations, and non-conformance inputs.    Make leakage, response, cleanliness, compatibility, lifetime, production repeatability, evidence gaps, delivery risks, and recovery options visible early.    Support MAIT/AIT preparation, integration, test procedures, acceptance evidence, flight-operations preparation, flight-data review, and abnormal-behaviour treatment for assigned fluidic equipment.    What We Would Love To See From You    Strong aerospace, mechanical, propulsion, fluids, or related engineering background.    Experience with spacecraft propulsion fluidic components such as valves, regulators, fill/drain equipment, pressure-control equipment, or related fluid-control hardware.    Practical understanding of requirements, verification, cleanliness, materials compatibility, leakage, actuation, testing, qualification, manufacturing support, and failure modes.    Ability to own technical supplier follow-up for complex hardware across requirements, interfaces, qualification, delivery, integration, and anomaly support.    Strong communication with propulsion, procurement, quality, MAIT/AIT, test, program, suppliers, manufacturing partners, and operations stakeholders.    Fluency in English; French and/or German are useful assets.    Skills And Behaviours    You keep the technical position clear even when ownership, supplier evidence, schedule, or integration constraints are messy.    You judge component decisions by spacecraft, mission, safety, integration, cost, and schedule impact.    You make evidence gaps, assumptions, weak test results, open points, and deviations visible early.    You balance fast development with configuration, cleanliness, verification, and qualification discipline.    You build trust with suppliers, partners, engineers, and leadership through facts and follow-through.     Why you should join us!   What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:      We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind     We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them      We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status.
